## Das erwartet Sie/dich
• Einblicke in spannende und dynamische Projekte an der Schnittstelle zwischen Patient:innenversorgung und universitärer Forschung (Koordination, Datenmanagement, Inhalt, etc.)
• Umgang mit Patient:innen im klinischen Umfeld: Unterstützung beim Ausfüllen von klinischen und psychologischen Fragebögen, Aufklärung über Inhalte und Ziele einer Studie

## Über uns
Die UDEM ist die grösste metabolische Klinik der Schweiz und vereint klinische Spitzenmedizin mit patientennaher Forschung. Ein Schwerpunkt liegt auf grossen klinischen Kohortenstudien wie der Swiss Obesity Study (SOS). Die Studie untersucht im klinischen Alltag die langfristigen Auswirkungen moderner medikamentöser Therapien bei Übergewicht und Adipositas auf die körperliche, psychische und soziale Gesundheit.
Im Rahmen dieser Projekte bieten wir Praktika für Studierende an (z.B. im Bereich Psychologie), die Freude an kommunikativen und präzisen Tätigkeiten haben.

jobs.description:
UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## What You Can Expect
You will join an active, supportive, inclusive, and collaborative research environment at the Department of Mathematics and Statistics. You will work on exciting fundamental questions at the interface of mathematics and modern AI and collaborate with national and international researchers. You will also contribute to teaching as a teaching assistant.
Employment conditions and remuneration are in accordance with the standards of the University of Bern, Switzerland.

## Profile of the Candidate
Applicants should hold, or be close to completing, a Master's degree in pure or applied mathematics, theoretical physics, statistics, or a related field.
We seek motivated candidates with a strong background in mathematics (e.g., in one or more of the following areas: analysis, probability theory, stochastic processes, statistical physics, optimal transport, dynamical systems, optimization, or machine learning theory), an interest in the mathematical principles underlying modern AI (or in related problems), the ability to work both independently and collaboratively, and good written and spoken English. Knowledge of German is not required. Programming experience is beneficial but not required.
International reputation
Application and Contact
Applications should include:
• a motivation letter (maximum one page);
• a curriculum vitae (maximum two pages);
• available BSc/MSc diplomas or academic transcripts;
• the names and contact details of one or two referees; and
• optional: a summary of the master's thesis (maximum two pages)
Evaluation of applications will continue until the position is filled. The exact starting date will be agreed upon with the successful candidate.

## About the Project
Modern artificial intelligence systems achieve remarkable performance, yet the mathematical mechanisms underlying their behavior remain only partially understood. This project seeks to develop a rigorous theory of modern learning algorithms and to explain how their architecture and dynamics determine their performance.
Depending on their background and interests, the candidate will use tools from analysis, probability theory, stochastic processes, statistical physics, dynamical systems, optimization, and optimal transport to prove mathematical results describing the behavior of modern learning algorithms in suitable abstract settings. Possible research directions include training dynamics and signal propagation in deep neural networks, including transformers; generative modeling; high-dimensional learning systems; sampling algorithms; collective phenomena in large-scale models; and quantum algorithms.
The work will be primarily theoretical. Computational experiments may be used to guide conjectures and illustrate theoretical results, depending on the candidate's interests.

descriptionByLocale.it:
UniBE è ambizioso.
Con noi, si offre le migliori prestazioni e testare le vostre abilità contro il meglio.

## Cosa si può aspettare
Ti unirai ad un ambiente di ricerca attivo, di supporto, inclusivo e collaborativo presso il Dipartimento di Matematica e Statistica. Si lavorerà su questioni fondamentali entusiasmanti all'interfaccia della matematica e dell'intelligenza artificiale moderna e collaborare con i ricercatori nazionali e internazionali. Contribuirai anche all'insegnamento come assistente di insegnamento.
Le condizioni di lavoro e la remunerazione sono conformi alle norme dell'Università di Berna, Svizzera.

## Profilo del candidato
I candidati devono tenere, o essere vicino al completamento, un master in matematica pura o applicata, fisica teorica, statistiche, o un campo correlato.
Cerchiamo candidati motivati con un forte background in matematica (ad esempio, in una o più delle seguenti aree: analisi, teoria delle probabilità, processi stocastici, fisica statistica, trasporto ottimale, sistemi dinamici, ottimizzazione, o teoria dell'apprendimento automatico), un interesse per i principi matematici sottostanti AI moderno (o in problemi correlati), la capacità di lavorare sia in modo indipendente e collaborativo, e buon inglese scritto e parlato. La conoscenza del tedesco non è richiesta. L'esperienza di programmazione è utile ma non richiesto.
reputazione internazionale
Applicazione e contatto
Le domande devono includere:
• una lettera di motivazione (massimo una pagina);
• un curriculum vitae (massimo due pagine);
• disponibili diplomi BSc/MSc o trascrizioni accademiche;
• i nomi e i dettagli di contatto di uno o due arbitri; e
• opzionale: un riassunto della tesi del maestro (massimo due pagine)
La revisione delle applicazioni inizierà nell'ultima settimana di agosto 2026 e continuerà fino a quando la posizione sarà riempita. La prima possibile data di inizio è ottobre 2026. La data di partenza esatta sarà concordata con il candidato di successo.

## Informazioni sul progetto
I moderni sistemi di intelligenza artificiale ottengono prestazioni notevoli, ma i meccanismi matematici sottostanti il loro comportamento rimangono solo parzialmente compresi. Questo progetto mira a sviluppare una rigorosa teoria degli algoritmi di apprendimento moderni e a spiegare come la loro architettura e dinamica determinano le loro prestazioni.
A seconda del loro background e interessi, il candidato utilizzerà strumenti da analisi, teoria delle probabilità, processi stocastici, fisica statistica, sistemi dinamici, ottimizzazione e trasporto ottimale per dimostrare risultati matematici che descrivono il comportamento degli algoritmi di apprendimento moderni in impostazioni astratti adeguate. Possibili direzioni di ricerca includono la dinamica di formazione e la propagazione del segnale nelle reti neurali profonde, compresi i trasformatori; la modellazione generativa; sistemi di apprendimento ad alta dimensione; algoritmi di campionamento; fenomeni collettivi nei modelli su larga scala; e algoritmi quantistici.
Il lavoro sarà principalmente teorico. Gli esperimenti computazionali possono essere utilizzati per guidare le congetture e illustrare i risultati teorici, a seconda degli interessi del candidato.

descriptionByLocale.de:
UniBE ist ehrgeizig.
Bei uns liefern Sie Spitzenleistungen und testen Ihre Fähigkeiten gegen die Besten.

## Was Sie erwarten können
Sie werden einer aktiven, unterstützenden, integrativen und kollaborativen Forschungsumgebung an der Abteilung für Mathematik und Statistik beitreten. Sie bearbeiten spannende Grundsatzfragen an der Schnittstelle von Mathematik und moderner KI und arbeiten mit nationalen und internationalen Forschern zusammen. Sie werden auch als Lehrassistent zum Unterrichten beitragen.
Beschäftigungsbedingungen und Vergütung entsprechen den Standards der Universität Bern, Schweiz.

## Profil des Kandidaten
Die Bewerber sollten einen Master-Abschluss in reiner oder angewandter Mathematik, theoretischer Physik, Statistik oder einem verwandten Gebiet haben oder kurz vor dem Abschluss stehen.
Wir suchen motivierte Kandidaten mit einem starken Hintergrund in Mathematik (z. B. in einem oder mehreren der folgenden Bereiche: Analyse, Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie, stochastische Prozesse, statistische Physik, optimaler Transport, dynamische Systeme, Optimierung oder maschinelle Lerntheorie), ein Interesse an den mathematischen Prinzipien, die der modernen KI zugrunde liegen (oder an verwandten Problemen), die Fähigkeit, sowohl unabhängig als auch kollaborativ zu arbeiten, und gutes geschriebenes und gesprochenes Englisch. Deutschkenntnisse sind nicht erforderlich. Programmiererfahrung ist vorteilhaft, aber nicht erforderlich.
Internationale Reputation
Bewerbung und Kontakt
Die Anträge sollten Folgendes umfassen:
• ein Motivationsschreiben (maximal eine Seite);
• Lebenslauf (höchstens zwei Seiten);
• verfügbare BSc / MSc-Diplome oder akademische Transkripte;
• die Namen und Kontaktdaten von einem oder zwei Schiedsrichtern und
• optional: Zusammenfassung der Masterarbeit (maximal zwei Seiten)
Die Überprüfung der Bewerbungen beginnt in der letzten Augustwoche 2026 und wird fortgesetzt, bis die Position besetzt ist. Der frühestmögliche Starttermin ist Oktober 2026. Der genaue Starttermin wird mit dem erfolgreichen Kandidaten vereinbart.

## Über das Projekt
Moderne Systeme der künstlichen Intelligenz erreichen eine bemerkenswerte Leistung, doch die mathematischen Mechanismen, die ihrem Verhalten zugrunde liegen, bleiben nur teilweise verstanden. Dieses Projekt zielt darauf ab, eine strenge Theorie moderner Lernalgorithmen zu entwickeln und zu erklären, wie ihre Architektur und Dynamik ihre Leistung bestimmen.
Je nach Hintergrund und Interessen wird der Kandidat Werkzeuge aus der Analyse, Wahrscheinlichkeitstheorie, stochastische Prozesse, statistische Physik, dynamische Systeme, Optimierung und optimalen Transport verwenden, um mathematische Ergebnisse zu beweisen, die das Verhalten moderner Lernalgorithmen in geeigneten abstrakten Einstellungen beschreiben. Mögliche Forschungsrichtungen umfassen Trainingsdynamik und Signalausbreitung in tiefen neuronalen Netzwerken, einschließlich Transformatoren; generative Modellierung; hochdimensionale Lernsysteme; Abtastalgorithmen; kollektive Phänomene in Großmodellen; und Quantenalgorithmen.
Die Arbeit wird in erster Linie theoretisch sein. Computerexperimente können verwendet werden, um Vermutungen zu leiten und theoretische Ergebnisse zu veranschaulichen, abhängig von den Interessen des Kandidaten.

Les demandes devraient comprendre :
• une lettre de motivation (maximum une page);
• un curriculum vitae (deux pages au maximum);
• les diplômes BSc/MSc disponibles ou les relevés de notes universitaires;
• les noms et coordonnées d'un ou de deux répondants;
• optionnel: un résumé de la thèse du maître (maximum deux pages)
L'examen des demandes commencera dans la dernière semaine d'août 2026 et se poursuivra jusqu'à ce que le poste soit comblé. La date de départ la plus rapprochée possible est octobre 2026. La date exacte de début sera convenue avec la candidate reçue.

## À propos du projet
Les systèmes modernes d'intelligence artificielle obtiennent des performances remarquables, mais les mécanismes mathématiques sous-jacents à leur comportement ne restent que partiellement compris. Ce projet vise à développer une théorie rigoureuse des algorithmes d'apprentissage modernes et à expliquer comment leur architecture et leur dynamique déterminent leur performance.
Selon leurs antécédents et leurs intérêts, le candidat utilisera des outils d'analyse, de théorie des probabilités, de processus stochastiques, de physique statistique, de systèmes dynamiques, d'optimisation et de transport optimal pour prouver des résultats mathématiques décrivant le comportement des algorithmes d'apprentissage modernes dans des paramètres abstraits appropriés. Les directions possibles de la recherche comprennent la dynamique de formation et la propagation des signaux dans les réseaux neuronaux profonds, y compris les transformateurs; la modélisation génératrice; les systèmes d'apprentissage à haute dimension; les algorithmes d'échantillonnage; les phénomènes collectifs dans les modèles à grande échelle; et les algorithmes quantiques.
Le travail sera essentiellement théorique. Des expériences informatiques peuvent être utilisées pour orienter les conjectures et illustrer les résultats théoriques, selon les intérêts du candidat.

## The Challenge
We are offering a PhD position to a highly motivated student. The research project investigates the impact of biomechanical stimulation, recreating the mechanical environment of bone tissue under physiological and dental surgical conditions, on cell-cell and cell-matrix interactions involved in early bone healing events. The project will utilize a variety of cell and molecular biological techniques to investigate molecular interactions that provide instructive cues for osteogenesis and osseointegration, with the aim of supporting personalized treatment approaches in dental implantology.

## Your Profile
• Master's degree in Cell or Molecular Biology. Candidates with a Master's degree in Dental Medicine will also be considered.
• Previous experience in cell culture techniques (primary and immortalized cells), as well as cell and molecular biological methods, is a strong asset.
• Additional experience in genomics, bioinformatics, imaging, and related image-analysis technologies is advantageous but not required.
• Excellent command of written and spoken English.
• Ability to work both under supervision and independently, while contributing to a collaborative team environment.

• Access to modern laboratory infrastructure and central university core facilities.
• The opportunity to contribute to highly translational research projects and to produce results of interest to a broad audience, ranging from basic researchers to clinicians in the fields of dental implantology, oral and maxillofacial surgery, and orthopedics.

## Die Herausforderung
Wir bieten einer hochmotivierten Person eine Doktoratsstelle an. Das Forschungsprojekt untersucht den Einfluss biomechanischer Stimulation, die die mechanische Umgebung des Knochengewebes unter physiologischen und zahnchirurgischen Bedingungen nachbildet, auf Zell-Zell- und Zell-Matrix-Interaktionen, die an frühen Ereignissen der Knochenheilung beteiligt sind. Im Rahmen des Projekts werden verschiedene zell- und molekularbiologische Techniken eingesetzt, um molekulare Interaktionen zu untersuchen, die instruktive Signale für Osteogenese und Osseointegration liefern, mit dem Ziel, personalisierte Behandlungsansätze in der dentalen Implantologie zu unterstützen.

jobs.description:
UniBE is interconnected.
With us, you're part of an international community and benefit from interdisciplinary collaboration.

## Tasks & 
• Requirements
We are looking for a motivated postdoctoral researcher who will lead the bioinformatic analyses of ancient plant DNA datasets. You will develop and adapt advanced bioinformatic tools and pipelines for individual-based ancient DNA (aDNA) data, as well as sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) metabarcoding and metagenomics. You will use these approaches to reconstruct changes in genetic diversity through time and investigate the genetic basis of adaptation to past environmental change. Furthermore, you will integrate paleogenomic data with population genetic models to test competing hypotheses about postglacial range expansion and demographic change in European tree species. You will collaborate with an interdisciplinary research team, provide scientific guidance to PhD and MSc students, present your findings at international conferences, and publish your results in leading peer-reviewed scientific journals.
You hold a PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, biology, or a related discipline and have a strong interest in applying computational methods to evolutionary and ecological questions. Substantial experience in bioinformatics, next-generation sequencing (NGS) data analysis, and ancient DNA research is essential. Programming skills (e.g. Python and R), as well as experience with command-line tools and high-performance computing clusters are expected. Knowledge of population genetics, paleoecology, molecular biology, or vegetation ecology is an asset. You approach your work with precision, creativity, and reliability, and have strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills. A proven track record of scientific publications and an excellent command of English are expected.

## 
• We offer
An exciting opportunity to work at the interface of bioinformatics, paleogenomics, and climate change research in a dynamic, international, and interdisciplinary research team at the University of Bern. Employment conditions follow the standards of the University of Bern and the SNSF.
Please submit a motivation letter, CV with publication list, academic transcripts, PhD diploma, and a reference letter and the contact details of your PhD supervisor as a single PDF file to Prof. Christoph Schwörer: christoph.schwoerer@unibe.ch. The application deadline is 1 December 2026. Applications received after this date may be considered until the position is filled. The University of Bern is committed to diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from candidates of all backgrounds. For further information contact Prof. Christoph Schwörer at the mentioned email.
Strong research infrastructure and international network
Application and Contact
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.
Within the framework of the SNSF Consolidator grant project ARIaDNA, a two-year postdoctoral research position is available at the Institute of Plant Sciences and the Oeschger Centre for Climate Change Research at the University of Bern, Switzerland . Paleogenomics & Vegetation Modelling. ARIaDNA aims to reconstruct how key European tree species responded to past environmental changes by analysing genetic data from ancient plant remains preserved in lake sediment archives. By combining paleogenomics, paleoecology, population genetics, and vegetation modelling, the project will generate new insights into postglacial forest dynamics, changes in genetic diversity, and climate adaptation, which will inform the conservation of alpine ecosystems under future climate change.

Sono previste competenze di programmazione (ad esempio Python e R), nonché esperienza con strumenti di linea di comando e cluster di calcolo ad alte prestazioni. La conoscenza della genetica della popolazione, della paleoecologia, della biologia molecolare o dell'ecologia della vegetazione è un bene. UniBE is interconnected.
With us, you're part of an international community and benefit from interdisciplinary collaboration.

## Tasks & 
• Requirements
We are looking for a motivated postdoctoral researcher who will lead the bioinformatic analyses of ancient plant DNA datasets. You will develop and adapt advanced bioinformatic tools and pipelines for individual-based ancient DNA (aDNA) data, as well as sedimentary ancient DNA (sedaDNA) metabarcoding and metagenomics. You will use these approaches to reconstruct changes in genetic diversity through time and investigate the genetic basis of adaptation to past environmental change. Furthermore, you will integrate paleogenomic data with population genetic models to test competing hypotheses about postglacial range expansion and demographic change in European tree species. You will collaborate with an interdisciplinary research team, provide scientific guidance to PhD and MSc students, present your findings at international conferences, and publish your results in leading peer-reviewed scientific journals.
You hold a PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, biology, or a related discipline and have a strong interest in applying computational methods to evolutionary and ecological questions. Substantial experience in bioinformatics, next-generation sequencing (NGS) data analysis, and ancient DNA research is essential. Programming skills (e.g. Python and R), as well as experience with command-line tools and high-performance computing clusters are expected. Knowledge of population genetics, paleoecology, molecular biology, or vegetation ecology is an asset. You approach your work with precision, creativity, and reliability, and have strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills. A proven track record of scientific publications and an excellent command of English are expected.

## 
• We offer
An exciting opportunity to work at the interface of bioinformatics, paleogenomics, and climate change research in a dynamic, international, and interdisciplinary research team at the University of Bern. Employment conditions follow the standards of the University of Bern and the SNSF.

ARIaDNA aims to reconstruct how key European tree species responded to past environmental changes by analysing genetic data from ancient plant remains preserved in lake sediment archives. By combining paleogenomics, paleoecology, population genetics, and vegetation modelling, the project will generate new insights into postglacial forest dynamics, changes in genetic diversity, and climate adaptation, which will inform the conservation of alpine ecosystems under future climate change.

jobs.description:
UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## About the project
Chronic diseases often develop gradually over years, and their trajectories vary widely between individuals. Understanding this progression is key to early detection and timely intervention. Large multimodal health datasets combining medical imaging, wearable sensor data and clinical measurements now make it possible to study disease progression from multiple perspectives.
The goal of this project is to develop machine learning methods that learn from multimodal health data to characterise and model disease progression. Methodological focus areas the candidate may explore include:
• Multimodal representation learning across imaging, time series and tabular data
• Disease progression modelling from cross-sectional and sparse longitudinal data
• Causal machine learning to disentangle disease progression from treatment effects
• Learning with missing modalities and irregularly sampled signals
• Fairness and bias in multimodal models across demographic subgroups

## The candidate
We are looking for a curious and motivated PhD candidate with a keen interest in doing machine learning research in the healthcare space. You should hold a Master's degree in a quantitative discipline such as computer science, machine learning, statistics, biomedical or electrical engineering, or similar. You have solid knowledge of the foundations of machine learning, are willing to dig deep to understand a problem, and have strong analytical skills. You have practical experience implementing and evaluating machine learning models in Python. Experience processing biomedical data (imaging, wearable, tabular) is a plus.
Strong research infrastructure and international network
Application and Contact
Applications received by 30 November 2026 will receive full consideration. After the deadline, we may continue to review applications until the position is filled.
Applications should include your CV, full transcripts (BSc and MSc), and a cover letter (max 1 page) telling us about your motivation and something you are particularly proud of or passionate about.
Please only apply through the portal (use the apply button below). Applications via email will not be considered or forwarded to the submission system.
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## About us
You will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Lisa Koch, head of the Machine Learning in Medicine Lab (www.mlm-lab.ch). Our research group develops trustworthy machine learning towards clinical use. Our methodological interests include uncertainty quantification, robustness and reliability, representation learning, probabilistic modelling, and causal machine learning, with applications in biomedical imaging, wearable and tabular data. We publish at leading machine learning and medical imaging venues, collaborate closely with clinicians at Inselspital, Bern University Hospital, and maintain close links to research groups across Switzerland and internationally.
We are a small and collaborative team and value regular interactions. Bern offers a strong and growing medical AI community and an excellent quality of life.

## Informazioni sul progetto
Le malattie croniche spesso si sviluppano gradualmente nel corso degli anni, e le loro traiettorie variano ampiamente tra gli individui. Capire questa progressione è fondamentale per il rilevamento precoce e l'intervento tempestivo. I grandi dataset di salute multimodale che combinano immagini mediche, dati dei sensori indossabili e misurazioni cliniche ora permettono di studiare progressione della malattia da più prospettive.
L'obiettivo di questo progetto è quello di sviluppare metodi di apprendimento automatico che imparano dai dati sanitari multimodali per caratterizzare e modellare la progressione della malattia. Le aree di messa a fuoco metodologico che il candidato può esplorare includono:
• Apprendimento di rappresentazione multimodale attraverso immagini, serie temporali e dati tabulari
• Modellazione progressiva della malattia da dati longitudinali trasversali e radi
• Macchina causale che impara a disentangle la progressione della malattia dagli effetti del trattamento
• Imparare con le modalità mancanti e i segnali a campione irregolare
• Fairness e bias in modelli multimodali attraverso sottogruppi demografici

## Il candidato
Stiamo cercando un candidato di dottorato curioso e motivato con un vivo interesse a fare ricerca di machine learning nello spazio sanitario. Si dovrebbe tenere un Master in una disciplina quantitativa come informatica, machine learning, statistiche, ingegneria biomedica o elettrica, o simili. Hai una solida conoscenza delle basi dell'apprendimento automatico, sono disposti a scavare in profondità per capire un problema, e hanno forti capacità analitiche. Hai esperienza pratica nell'implementazione e nella valutazione dei modelli di machine learning in Python. L'esperienza di elaborazione dati biomedici (imaging, indossabile, tabulare) è un plus.
Forte infrastruttura di ricerca e rete internazionale
Applicazione e contatto
Le domande ricevute entro il 30 novembre 2026 riceveranno piena considerazione. Dopo la scadenza, possiamo continuare a rivedere le applicazioni fino a quando la posizione è piena.
Le domande dovrebbero includere il vostro CV, trascrizioni complete (BSc e MSc), e una lettera di copertura (max 1 pagina) che ci racconta la vostra motivazione e qualcosa di cui siete particolarmente orgogliosi o appassionati.
Con noi, crei valore.
Per te e per la società.

## Informazioni su di noi
Sarà supervisionato dal Prof. Dr. Lisa Koch, responsabile del Machine Learning in Medicine Lab (www.mlm-lab.ch). Il nostro gruppo di ricerca sviluppa l'apprendimento automatico affidabile verso l'uso clinico. I nostri interessi metodologici includono la quantificazione dell'incertezza, la robustezza e l'affidabilità, l'apprendimento delle rappresentazioni, la modellazione probabilistica e l'apprendimento delle macchine causali, con applicazioni in imaging biomedico, dati indossabili e tabulari. Pubblichiamo presso le principali sedi di machine learning e di imaging medicale, collaboriamo a stretto contatto con i medici dell'Inselspital, dell'ospedale universitario di Berna, e manteniamo stretti legami con i gruppi di ricerca in tutta la Svizzera e a livello internazionale.
Siamo un team piccolo e collaborativo e valutiamo le interazioni regolari. Berna offre una forte e crescente comunità di AI medica e un'eccellente qualità di vita.

UniBE ist ehrgeizig.
Bei uns liefern Sie Spitzenleistungen und testen Ihre Fähigkeiten gegen die Besten.

## Über das Projekt
Chronische Krankheiten entwickeln sich oft allmählich über Jahre, und ihre Trajektorien variieren stark zwischen Individuen. Das Verständnis dieser Progression ist der Schlüssel zur Früherkennung und rechtzeitigen Intervention. Große multimodale Gesundheitsdatensätze, die medizinische Bildgebung, tragbare Sensordaten und klinische Messungen kombinieren, ermöglichen es nun, den Krankheitsverlauf aus mehreren Perspektiven zu untersuchen.
Ziel dieses Projekts ist es, maschinelle Lernmethoden zu entwickeln, die aus multimodalen Gesundheitsdaten lernen, um das Fortschreiten der Krankheit zu charakterisieren und zu modellieren. Methodische Schwerpunktbereiche, die der Kandidat erkunden kann, umfassen:
• Multimodales Repräsentationslernen über Bildgebung, Zeitreihen und Tabellendaten
• Krankheitsprogressionsmodellierung aus Querschnitts- und spärlichen Längsschnittdaten
• Kausales maschinelles Lernen, um Krankheitsprogression von Behandlungseffekten zu entwirren
• Lernen mit fehlenden Modalitäten und unregelmäßig abgetasteten Signalen
• Fairness und Bias in multimodalen Modellen über demografische Untergruppen hinweg

## Der Kandidat
Wir suchen einen neugierigen und motivierten Doktoranden mit einem großen Interesse an maschineller Lernforschung im Gesundheitswesen. Sie sollten einen Master-Abschluss in einer quantitativen Disziplin wie Informatik, maschinelles Lernen, Statistik, biomedizinische oder Elektrotechnik oder ähnliches haben. Sie haben solide Kenntnisse der Grundlagen des maschinellen Lernens, sind bereit, tief zu graben, um ein Problem zu verstehen, und haben starke analytische Fähigkeiten. Sie haben praktische Erfahrung in der Implementierung und Bewertung von Machine Learning-Modellen in Python. Erfahrung in der Verarbeitung biomedizinischer Daten (imaging, wearable, tabellarisch) ist ein Plus.
Starke Forschungsinfrastruktur und internationales Netzwerk
Bewerbung und Kontakt
Anträge, die bis zum 30. November 2026 eingehen, werden in vollem Umfang berücksichtigt. Nach Ablauf der Frist können wir weiterhin Anträge prüfen, bis die Position besetzt ist.
Bewerbungen sollten Ihren Lebenslauf, vollständige Transkripte (BSc und MSc) und ein Anschreiben (max. 1 Seite) enthalten, das uns über Ihre Motivation und etwas, auf das Sie besonders stolz oder leidenschaftlich sind, informiert.
Mit uns schaffen Sie Werte.
Für dich und für die Gesellschaft.

## Über uns
Sie werden betreut von Prof. Dr. Lisa Koch, Leiterin des Machine Learning in Medicine Lab (www.mlm-lab.ch). Unsere Forschungsgruppe entwickelt vertrauenswürdiges maschinelles Lernen für den klinischen Einsatz. Unsere methodischen Interessen umfassen Unsicherheitsquantifizierung, Robustheit und Zuverlässigkeit, Repräsentationslernen, probabilistische Modellierung und kausales maschinelles Lernen mit Anwendungen in der biomedizinischen Bildgebung, tragbaren und tabellarischen Daten. Wir publizieren an führenden Orten für maschinelles Lernen und medizinische Bildgebung, arbeiten eng mit Klinikern im Inselspital des Universitätsklinikums Bern zusammen und pflegen enge Verbindungen zu Forschungsgruppen in der Schweiz und international.
Wir sind ein kleines und kollaboratives Team und schätzen regelmäßige Interaktionen. Bern bietet eine starke und wachsende medizinische KI-Community und eine ausgezeichnete Lebensqualität.

## A propos du projet
Les maladies chroniques se développent souvent progressivement au fil des ans, et leurs trajectoires varient grandement d'un individu à l'autre. De grands ensembles de données multimodales sur la santé combinant l'imagerie médicale, les données de capteurs portables et les mesures cliniques permettent désormais d'étudier la progression de la maladie sous de multiples perspectives.
L'objectif de ce projet est de développer des méthodes d'apprentissage automatique qui apprennent à partir de données de santé multimodales pour caractériser et modéliser la progression des maladies. Les domaines d'intérêt méthodologiques que le candidat peut explorer comprennent :
• Apprentissage de la représentation multimodale à travers l'imagerie, les séries chronologiques et les données tabulaires
• Modélisation de la progression de la maladie à partir de données longitudinales transversales et éparses
• Apprentissage automatique causal pour démêler la progression de la maladie des effets du traitement
• Apprendre avec des modalités manquantes et des signaux échantillonnés irrégulièrement
• Équité et biais dans les modèles multimodaux des sous-groupes démographiques

## Le candidat
Nous sommes à la recherche d'un candidat au doctorat curieux et motivé qui s'intéresse vivement à la recherche en apprentissage automatique dans l'espace des soins de santé. UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## 
• Profile
We are looking for a creative and motivated candidate, a team player, with a MSc degree in physics, chemistry, or biology. Willingness to learn microbiological techniques is essential; prior wet lab experience is an asset. No prior expertise in optics is required; training will be provided, though a basic understanding of polarization, vacuum technology and/or mass spectrometry is a plus. Excellent oral and written skills in English are a requirement.

## 
• What we offer
The position is based at the Centre for Space and Habitability, which strives to investigate key questions in space sciences through interdisciplinarity. The team collaborates tightly with various national and international partners. This includes for example the Microbiology Laboratory of the University of Neuchâtel where the lab measurements on microorganisms will be conducted. Laser-based mass spectrometry on organics will be conducted at the Space Research and Planetary Sciences division of the University of Bern, which is closely collaborating with colleagues at NASA Ames Research Center, USA.
The city of Bern is well known for its quality of life, cultural richness and beautiful surroundings offering plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities.
The position is funded for a period of 4 years. The annual gross salary is competitive, ranging from CHF 50,042 in the first year to CHF 53,263 in the final year. Ample funding for travel, publications and computing resources will be available. Child allowance and maternity/paternity leave are offered. Assistance with visa procedures is available for international candidates. Additionally, the CSH offers career advice, mentorship, and teaching opportunities.
International reputation
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## NCCR Genesis: background
The Centre for Space and Habitability (CSH) and the Division for Space Research and Planetary Sciences (WP) at the University of Bern invite applications for a PhD position in the frame of the new NCCR Genesis.
The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect unambiguous traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress.
Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website https://nccr-genesis.ch.
Our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion
NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups.
Project description
Are we alone in the universe? The search for life beyond the Earth is one of the most fascinating endeavours that humankind has embarked upon. Recent years have seen tremendous progress in instrumentation, laboratory experiments and theories on the origin of life.
This PhD project will investigate for the first time the combination of remote life sensing techniques using circular spectro-polarimetry with in situ laser-based mass spectrometry measurements, both designed for the detection or signatures of life. The work will mainly involve experiments in the lab, using cell cultures of a range of strains (including anaerobic cultivation of microorganisms) and various classes of organic molecules relevant to Solar System environments. These studies will be complemented by targeted field measurements of soil material containing microorganisms and low abundant organics that are relevant candidates for extinct/extant life on Mars or in the icy moons of the solar system. The results of this endeavour will reveal the potential of combining life detection methods at different scales that will be key to define optimal strategies for future life-detection missions, such as the planned ESA L4 mission to Enceladus or future NASA mission to Mars.
The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team with expertise spanning astrophysics, microbiology, biomedicine and engineering. The new group member will have the opportunity to gain unique experience in dual-use instrumentation applicable to both space exploration and medical diagnostics.

UniBE è ambizioso.
Con noi, si offre le migliori prestazioni e testare le vostre abilità contro il meglio.

##
• Profilo
Stiamo cercando un candidato creativo e motivato, un giocatore di squadra, con una laurea in fisica, chimica o biologia. La volontà di imparare le tecniche microbiologiche è essenziale; prima esperienza di laboratorio umido è un bene. Non è richiesta alcuna esperienza preliminare nell'ottica; sarà fornita una formazione, anche se una comprensione di base della polarizzazione, la tecnologia del vuoto e/o la spettrometria di massa è un plus. Le eccellenti abilità orali e scritte in inglese sono un requisito.

##
• Cosa offriamo
La posizione si basa sul Centre for Space and Habitability, che si sforza di indagare le questioni chiave nelle scienze spaziali attraverso l'interdisciplinarità. Il team collabora strettamente con vari partner nazionali e internazionali. Questo include, ad esempio, il Laboratorio di Microbiologia dell'Università di Neuchâtel dove saranno condotte le misurazioni di laboratorio sui microrganismi. La spettrometria di massa basata sul laser sugli organici sarà condotta presso la divisione Space Research and Planetary Sciences dell'Università di Berna, che sta collaborando strettamente con i colleghi della NASA Ames Research Center, USA.
La città di Berna è ben nota per la sua qualità di vita, ricchezza culturale e un bellissimo ambiente che offre molte opportunità per le attività all'aperto.
La posizione è finanziata per un periodo di 4 anni. Lo stipendio lordo annuale è competitivo, che va da CHF 50.042 nel primo anno a CHF 53.263 nell'ultimo anno. Saranno disponibili numerosi finanziamenti per viaggi, pubblicazioni e risorse di calcolo. Sono offerti assegni per bambini e congedo di maternità/paternità. L'assistenza con procedure di visto è disponibile per i candidati internazionali. Inoltre, il CSH offre consigli di carriera, mentore e opportunità di insegnamento.
reputazione internazionale
Con noi, crei valore.
Per te e per la società.

## Genesi NCCR: sfondo
Il Centre for Space and Habitability (CSH) e la Divisione Ricerca Spaziale e Scienze Planetarie (WP) presso l'Università di Berna invitano le domande per una posizione di dottorato nella cornice della nuova Genesi NCCR.
Il National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis è un progetto di infrastruttura di ricerca finanziato da SNSF che si concentra sull'esplorazione dell'emergere della vita nell'universo. Questa infrastruttura di ricerca interdisciplinare riunisce fisici, scienziati terrestri e planetari, chimici e biologi per comprendere le condizioni e i meccanismi che permettono alla vita di emergere. Lo sviluppo di metodi affidabili per rilevare tracce di vita non ambigue (biosignatures) – sia attraverso il telerilevamento o le misurazioni dirette in loco – richiede una significativa innovazione. Queste sfide richiedono una stretta collaborazione tra fisica, biologia, chimica e scienze della terra. NCCR Genesis non mira a fornire risposte in tutti i campi, ma a guidare la ricerca innovativa e raggiungere un progresso decisivo.
I dettagli sulla genesi NCCR sono disponibili sul suo sito web https://nccr-genesis.ch.
Il nostro impegno per l'uguaglianza, la diversità e l'inclusione
NCCR Genesis è profondamente impegnata per l'uguaglianza, la diversità e l'inclusione. Il nostro obiettivo è quello di coltivare una cultura del lavoro rispettosa ed equa con uguale accesso allo sviluppo professionale e al supporto per tutti. Noi incoraggiamo fortemente le applicazioni da gruppi sottorappresentati.
Descrizione del progetto
Siamo soli nell'universo? La ricerca della vita al di là della Terra è uno degli sforzi più affascinanti che l'umanità ha intrapreso. Gli ultimi anni hanno visto enormi progressi nella strumentazione, negli esperimenti di laboratorio e nelle teorie sull'origine della vita.
Questo progetto PhD studierà per la prima volta la combinazione di tecniche di rilevamento della vita remota utilizzando spettro-polarimetria circolare con misurazioni di spettrometria di massa basate sul laser situ, entrambe progettate per il rilevamento o la firma della vita. Il lavoro coinvolgerà principalmente esperimenti in laboratorio, utilizzando culture cellulari di una gamma di ceppi (compresa la coltivazione anaerobica di microrganismi) e varie classi di molecole organiche rilevanti per gli ambienti del Sistema Solare. Questi studi saranno completati da misure mirate sul campo di materiale del suolo che contengono microrganismi e bassi organici abbondanti che sono candidati rilevanti per la vita estinta / esistente su Marte o nelle lune ghiacciate del sistema solare. I risultati di questo sforzo riveleranno il potenziale di combinare metodi di rilevamento della vita a diverse scale che saranno la chiave per definire strategie ottimali per future missioni di rilevamento della vita, come la missione prevista ESA L4 per Enceladus o la futura missione della NASA per Marte.
Il candidato di successo si unirà a un team interdisciplinare con competenze che spaziano astrofisica, microbiologia, biomedicina e ingegneria. Il nuovo membro del gruppo avrà l'opportunità di acquisire un'esperienza unica nella strumentazione a doppio uso applicabile sia all'esplorazione spaziale che alla diagnostica medica.

Diese Herausforderungen erfordern eine enge Zusammenarbeit zwischen Physik, Biologie, Chemie und den Geowissenschaften. Der NFS Genesis will nicht in allen Bereichen Antworten liefern, sondern innovative Forschung vorantreiben und entscheidende Fortschritte erzielen.
Details zum NFS Genesis sind auf seiner Website https://nccr-genesis.ch verfügbar.
Unser Engagement für Gleichheit, Vielfalt und Inklusion
Der NFS Genesis setzt sich für Gleichheit, Vielfalt und Inklusion ein. Unser Ziel ist es, eine respektvolle und faire Arbeitskultur mit gleichem Zugang zu beruflicher Entwicklung und Unterstützung für alle zu pflegen. Wir empfehlen dringend Bewerbungen von unterrepräsentierten Gruppen.
Projektbeschreibung
Sind wir allein im Universum? Die Suche nach Leben jenseits der Erde ist eine der faszinierendsten Bemühungen, die die Menschheit unternommen hat. In den letzten Jahren gab es enorme Fortschritte bei der Instrumentierung, Laborexperimenten und Theorien über den Ursprung des Lebens.
Dieses PhD-Projekt wird zum ersten Mal die Kombination von Fernerkundungsverfahren unter Verwendung von Zirkularspektropolarimetrie mit in-situ-laserbasierten Massenspektrometriemessungen untersuchen, die sowohl für die Detektion als auch für Signaturen von Leben konzipiert sind. Die Arbeit wird hauptsächlich Experimente im Labor umfassen, bei denen Zellkulturen einer Reihe von Stämmen (einschließlich der anaeroben Kultivierung von Mikroorganismen) und verschiedene Klassen von organischen Molekülen verwendet werden, die für die Umgebung des Sonnensystems relevant sind. Diese Studien werden durch gezielte Feldmessungen von Bodenmaterial ergänzt, das Mikroorganismen und wenig häufig vorkommende organische Stoffe enthält, die relevante Kandidaten für ausgestorbenes / vorhandenes Leben auf dem Mars oder in den eisigen Monden des Sonnensystems sind. Die Ergebnisse dieses Vorhabens werden das Potenzial der Kombination von Methoden zur Entdeckung von Leben in verschiedenen Größenordnungen aufzeigen, die für die Festlegung optimaler Strategien für zukünftige Missionen zur Entdeckung von Leben, wie die geplante ESA L4-Mission nach Enceladus oder die zukünftige NASA-Mission zum Mars, von entscheidender Bedeutung sein werden.
Der erfolgreiche Kandidat wird sich einem interdisziplinären Team mit Fachkenntnissen aus den Bereichen Astrophysik, Mikrobiologie, Biomedizin und Technik anschließen. Das neue Gruppenmitglied wird die Möglichkeit haben, einzigartige Erfahrungen mit Dual-Use-Instrumenten zu sammeln, die sowohl für die Weltraumforschung als auch für die medizinische Diagnostik geeignet sind.

UniBE est ambitieux.
Avec nous, vous offrez des performances supérieures et testez vos compétences contre les meilleurs.

##
• Profil
Nous recherchons un candidat créatif et motivé, un joueur d'équipe, avec un diplôme de maîtrise en physique, en chimie ou en biologie. La volonté d'apprendre des techniques microbiologiques est essentielle; l'expérience préalable en laboratoire humide est un atout. Aucune expertise préalable en optique n'est requise; une formation sera dispensée, bien qu'une compréhension de base de la polarisation, de la technologie du vide et/ou de la spectrométrie de masse soit un atout. Excellentes compétences orales et écrites en anglais sont une exigence.

##
• Ce que nous offrons
Le poste est situé au Centre for Space and Habitability, qui s'efforce d'étudier des questions clés en sciences spatiales par l'interdisciplinarité. L'équipe collabore étroitement avec divers partenaires nationaux et internationaux. Cela inclut par exemple le Laboratoire de microbiologie de l'Université de Neuchâtel où les mesures de laboratoire sur les microorganismes seront effectuées. La spectrométrie de masse à base de laser sur l'organique sera réalisée à la division de recherche spatiale et des sciences planétaires de l'Université de Berne, qui collabore étroitement avec des collègues du Centre de recherche Ames de la NASA, aux États-Unis.
La ville de Berne est bien connue pour sa qualité de vie, sa richesse culturelle et son environnement magnifique offrant de nombreuses possibilités d'activités de plein air.
Le poste est financé pour une période de 4 ans. Le salaire annuel brut est compétitif, allant de 50 042 CHF la première année à 53 263 CHF la dernière année. De nombreux fonds seront disponibles pour les voyages, les publications et les ressources informatiques. Des allocations familiales et des congés de maternité/paternité sont offerts. Une assistance aux procédures de visa est disponible pour les candidats internationaux. De plus, le CSH offre des conseils professionnels, du mentorat et des possibilités d'enseignement.
La réputation internationale
Avec nous, vous créez de la valeur.
Pour vous et pour la société.

## NCR Genèse: contexte
Le Centre for Space and Habitability (CSH) et la Division de la recherche spatiale et des sciences planétaires (WP) de l'Université de Berne invitent les candidats à un doctorat dans le cadre de la nouvelle Genèse du NCCR.
Le Centre national de compétence en recherche NCCR Genesis est un projet d'infrastructure de recherche financé par la SNSF qui vise à explorer l'émergence de la vie dans l'Univers. Cette infrastructure de recherche interdisciplinaire rassemble des physiciens, des scientifiques de la terre et de la planète, des chimistes et des biologistes pour comprendre les conditions et les mécanismes qui permettent à la vie d' émerger. Le développement de méthodes fiables pour détecter des traces de vie sans ambiguïté (biosignatures) – que ce soit par télédétection ou par des mesures directes sur place – nécessite une innovation significative. Ces défis exigent une collaboration étroite entre la physique, la biologie, la chimie et les sciences de la terre. NCCR Genesis n'a pas pour but de fournir des réponses dans tous les domaines, mais de stimuler la recherche innovante et de réaliser des progrès décisifs.
Des renseignements sur la genèse du CCNR sont disponibles sur son site Web https://nccr-genesis.ch.
Notre engagement en faveur de l'égalité, de la diversité et de l'inclusion
Le CCNR Genesis est profondément attaché à l'égalité, à la diversité et à l'inclusion. Notre objectif est de cultiver une culture du travail respectueuse et équitable avec un accès égal au perfectionnement professionnel et au soutien pour tous. Nous encourageons vivement les demandes émanant de groupes sous-représentés.
Description du projet
Sommes-nous seuls dans l'univers ? La recherche de la vie au-delà de la Terre est l'une des plus fascinantes entreprises par l'humanité. Ces dernières années ont vu des progrès considérables dans l'instrumentation, les expériences de laboratoire et les théories sur l'origine de la vie.
Ce projet de doctorat étudiera pour la première fois la combinaison de techniques de télédétection utilisant la spectropolarimétrie circulaire avec des mesures de spectrométrie de masse au laser in situ, toutes deux conçues pour la détection ou la signature de la vie. Le travail comprendra principalement des expériences en laboratoire, utilisant des cultures cellulaires d'une gamme de souches (y compris la culture anaérobie de microorganismes) et diverses classes de molécules organiques pertinentes pour les environnements du système solaire. Ces études seront complétées par des mesures ciblées sur le terrain des matériaux du sol contenant des microorganismes et des organiques peu abondants qui sont des candidats pertinents pour la vie éteinte/existante sur Mars ou dans les lunes glacées du système solaire. Les résultats de cette initiative révéleront le potentiel de combiner des méthodes de détection de la vie à différentes échelles qui seront essentielles pour définir des stratégies optimales pour les futures missions de détection de la vie, comme la mission L4 de l'ESA à Encelade ou la future mission de la NASA à Mars.
Le candidat retenu se joindra à une équipe interdisciplinaire ayant une expertise en astrophysique, en microbiologie, en biomédecine et en génie. Le nouveau membre du groupe aura l'occasion d'acquérir une expérience unique en matière d'instrumentation à double usage applicable à la fois à l'exploration spatiale et au diagnostic médical.

Our team collaborates tightly with the Microbiology Laboratory (Prof. Pilar Junier) of the University of Neuchâtel where the lab measurements are conducted. The city of Bern is well known for its quality of life, cultural richness and beautiful surroundings offering plenty of opportunities for outdoor activities.
The position is funded for a period of 4 years. The annual gross salary is competitive, ranging from CHF 50,042 in the first year to CHF 53,263 in the final year. International reputation

For yourself and for society.

## NCCR Genesis: background
The Centre for Space and Habitability (CSH) at the University of Bern invites applications for a PhD position in the frame of the new NCCR Genesis.
The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect unambiguous traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress.
Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website https://nccr-genesis.ch.
Our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion
NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups.
Project description
Are we alone in the universe? The search for life beyond the Earth is one of the most fascinating endeavours that humankind has embarked upon. Recent years have seen tremendous progress in instrumentation, laboratory experiments and theories on the origin of life.
This PhD project will investigate the impact of icy-moon environmental conditions on the detectability of selected bacteria in ice/salt mixtures rapidly exposed to vacuum, extremely low temperatures and high-radiation levels. For this purpose, a high-sensitivity spectro-polarimeter will be interfaced with a temperature-vacuum chamber. Additionally, an electron gun and a UV light source will be used to investigate the incidence of harsh conditions on bacterial samples deposited on ice as a proxy for icy moon conditions. The study will also investigate whether spectro-polarimetry could probe fundamental structures in the microorganisms such as cofactors or proteins in the near UV. The project will thus investigate the detectability of fundamental biosignatures relevant to a wider range of microorganisms. This effort will inform the preparation of future life-detection missions in our Solar System, such as the planned ESA L4 mission to Enceladus.
The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team (lead: Prof. Brice-Olivier Demory) with expertise spanning astrophysics, microbiology, biomedicine and engineering. The new group member will have the opportunity to gain unique experience in dual-use instrumentation applicable to both space exploration and medical diagnostics.

## Genesi NCCR: sfondo
Il Centre for Space and Habitability (CSH) dell'Università di Berna invita le domande di una posizione di dottorato nel quadro della nuova Genesi NCCR.
Il National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis è un progetto di infrastruttura di ricerca finanziato da SNSF che si concentra sull'esplorazione dell'emergere della vita nell'universo. Questa infrastruttura di ricerca interdisciplinare riunisce fisici, scienziati terrestri e planetari, chimici e biologi per comprendere le condizioni e i meccanismi che permettono alla vita di emergere. Lo sviluppo di metodi affidabili per rilevare tracce di vita non ambigue (biosignatures) – sia attraverso il telerilevamento o le misurazioni dirette in loco – richiede una significativa innovazione. Queste sfide richiedono una stretta collaborazione tra fisica, biologia, chimica e scienze della terra. NCCR Genesis non mira a fornire risposte in tutti i campi, ma a guidare la ricerca innovativa e raggiungere un progresso decisivo.
I dettagli sulla genesi NCCR sono disponibili sul suo sito web https://nccr-genesis.ch.
Il nostro impegno per l'uguaglianza, la diversità e l'inclusione
NCCR Genesis è profondamente impegnata per l'uguaglianza, la diversità e l'inclusione. Il nostro obiettivo è quello di coltivare una cultura del lavoro rispettosa ed equa con uguale accesso allo sviluppo professionale e al supporto per tutti. Noi incoraggiamo fortemente le applicazioni da gruppi sottorappresentati.
Descrizione del progetto
Siamo soli nell'universo? La ricerca della vita al di là della Terra è uno degli sforzi più affascinanti che l'umanità ha intrapreso. Gli ultimi anni hanno visto enormi progressi nella strumentazione, negli esperimenti di laboratorio e nelle teorie sull'origine della vita.
Questo progetto PhD studierà l'impatto delle condizioni ambientali icy-moon sulla rilevabilità dei batteri selezionati in miscele di ghiaccio/sale rapidamente esposti al vuoto, temperature estremamente basse e livelli di alta radiazione. Con questo scopo, uno spettro-polarimetro ad alta sensibilità verrà interfacciato con una camera a vuoto. Inoltre, un elettrone e una fonte di luce UV saranno utilizzati per indagare l'incidenza di condizioni dure su campioni batterici depositati sul ghiaccio come proxy per le condizioni di luna gelida. Lo studio studierà anche se la spettro-polarimetria potrebbe sondare strutture fondamentali nei microrganismi come i cofattori o le proteine nel vicino UV. Il progetto indicherà quindi la rilevabilità delle biofirme fondamentali rilevanti per una più ampia gamma di microrganismi. Questo sforzo informerà la preparazione delle future missioni di rilevamento della vita nel nostro Sistema Solare, come la prevista missione ESA L4 ad Enceladus.
Il candidato di successo si unirà a un team interdisciplinare (capo: Prof. Brice-Olivier Demory) con competenze che spaziano dall'astrofisica, dalla microbiologia, dalla biomedicina e dall'ingegneria. Il nuovo membro del gruppo avrà l'opportunità di acquisire un'esperienza unica nella strumentazione a doppio uso applicabile sia all'esplorazione spaziale che alla diagnostica medica.

Zusätzlich werden eine Elektronenkanone und eine UV-Lichtquelle verwendet, um das Auftreten von harten Bedingungen auf Bakterienproben zu untersuchen, die auf Eis als Stellvertreter für eisige Mondbedingungen abgelagert werden. Die Studie wird auch untersuchen, ob die Spektropolarimetrie grundlegende Strukturen in den Mikroorganismen wie Cofaktoren oder Proteine im nahen UV untersuchen könnte. Das Projekt wird somit die Nachweisbarkeit grundlegender Biosignaturen untersuchen, die für ein breiteres Spektrum von Mikroorganismen relevant sind. Diese Bemühungen werden die Vorbereitung zukünftiger Lebenserkennungsmissionen in unserem Sonnensystem beeinflussen, wie die geplante ESA L4-Mission nach Enceladus.
Der erfolgreiche Kandidat wird sich einem interdisziplinären Team anschließen (Leiter: Prof. Brice-Olivier Demory) mit Fachkenntnissen aus den Bereichen Astrophysik, Mikrobiologie, Biomedizin und Technik. Das neue Gruppenmitglied wird die Möglichkeit haben, einzigartige Erfahrungen mit Dual-Use-Instrumenten zu sammeln, die sowohl für die Weltraumforschung als auch für die medizinische Diagnostik geeignet sind.

##
• Ce que nous offrons
Le poste est situé au Centre for Space and Habitability, qui s'efforce d'étudier des questions clés en sciences spatiales par l'interdisciplinarité. Notre équipe collabore étroitement avec le Laboratoire de microbiologie (Prof. Pilar Junier) de l'Université de Neuchâtel où les mesures de laboratoire sont effectuées. La ville de Berne est bien connue pour sa qualité de vie, sa richesse culturelle et son environnement magnifique offrant de nombreuses possibilités d'activités de plein air.
Le poste est financé pour une période de 4 ans. Le salaire annuel brut est compétitif, allant de 50 042 CHF la première année à 53 263 CHF la dernière année. De nombreux fonds seront disponibles pour les voyages, les publications et les ressources informatiques. Des allocations familiales et des congés de maternité/paternité sont offerts. Une assistance aux procédures de visa est disponible pour les candidats internationaux. De plus, le CSH offre des conseils professionnels, du mentorat et des possibilités d'enseignement.
La réputation internationale
Avec nous, vous créez de la valeur.
Pour vous et pour la société.

## NCR Genèse: contexte
Le Centre for Space and Habitability (CSH) de l'Université de Berne invite les candidats à un doctorat dans le cadre de la nouvelle Genèse du CCNR.
Le Centre national de compétence en recherche NCCR Genesis est un projet d'infrastructure de recherche financé par la SNSF qui vise à explorer l'émergence de la vie dans l'Univers. Cette infrastructure de recherche interdisciplinaire rassemble des physiciens, des scientifiques de la terre et de la planète, des chimistes et des biologistes pour comprendre les conditions et les mécanismes qui permettent à la vie d' émerger. Le développement de méthodes fiables pour détecter des traces de vie sans ambiguïté (biosignatures) – que ce soit par télédétection ou par des mesures directes sur place – nécessite une innovation significative. Ces défis exigent une collaboration étroite entre la physique, la biologie, la chimie et les sciences de la terre. NCCR Genesis n'a pas pour but de fournir des réponses dans tous les domaines, mais de stimuler la recherche innovante et de réaliser des progrès décisifs.
Des renseignements sur la genèse du CCNR sont disponibles sur son site Web https://nccr-genesis.ch.
Notre engagement en faveur de l'égalité, de la diversité et de l'inclusion
Le CCNR Genesis est profondément attaché à l'égalité, à la diversité et à l'inclusion. Notre objectif est de cultiver une culture du travail respectueuse et équitable avec un accès égal au perfectionnement professionnel et au soutien pour tous. Nous encourageons vivement les demandes émanant de groupes sous-représentés.
Description du projet
Sommes-nous seuls dans l'univers ? La recherche de la vie au-delà de la Terre est l'une des plus fascinantes entreprises par l'humanité. Ces dernières années ont vu des progrès considérables dans l'instrumentation, les expériences de laboratoire et les théories sur l'origine de la vie.
Ce projet de doctorat étudiera l'impact des conditions environnementales de la lune glacée sur la détectabilité de certaines bactéries dans des mélanges de glace et de sel rapidement exposées au vide, à des températures extrêmement basses et à des niveaux de rayonnement élevés. À cette fin, un spectropolarimètre à haute sensibilité sera interfacé avec une chambre température-vacuum. De plus, un pistolet à électrons et une source de lumière UV seront utilisés pour étudier l'incidence de conditions difficiles sur les échantillons bactériens déposés sur la glace comme substitut des conditions de lune glacée. L'étude permettra également d'étudier si la spectropolarimétrie pourrait sonder les structures fondamentales des microorganismes tels que les cofacteurs ou les protéines dans le proche UV. Le projet étudiera donc la détectabilité des biosignatures fondamentales pertinentes pour un éventail plus large de micro-organismes. Cet effort éclairera la préparation de futures missions de détection de la vie dans notre système solaire, comme la mission prévue de l'ESA L4 à Encelade.
Le candidat retenu se joindra à une équipe interdisciplinaire (chef de file : Prof. Brice-Olivier Demory) avec une expertise en astrophysique, en microbiologie, en biomédecine et en génie. Le nouveau membre du groupe aura l'occasion d'acquérir une expérience unique en matière d'instrumentation à double usage applicable à la fois à l'exploration spatiale et au diagnostic médical.

jobs.description:
UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## Your tasks and what we offer
Develop your research line and participate in project activities. This includes
• working in archives;
• clarifying rights and potential ethical issues;
• communicating with archivists and authors/rights holders;
• working with legacy hardware and software, using digital forensics methods;
• studying the writing process of authors across different media;
• studying archival materials such as unpublished texts and drafts of publications;
• publishing and presenting your work locally and internationally;
• contributing to the organisation of scholarly events;
• collaborating with the rest of the team.
Participation in teaching is optional. The starting date is March 2027, with flexibility for a later start.
What we offer
• A dynamic and collaborative research environment at the Digital Humanities unit.
• Work-life balance through flexible work schedules.
• Training opportunities in all areas of the project and related fields.
• Salary according to SNSF regulations.

## Candidate profile
PhD in textual scholarship (philology, textual criticism, scholarly editing, genetic criticism) or literary studies or digital humanities.
• Prior experience in working with archives.
• Prior experience or strong interest in contemporary Swiss French and/or Italian literature; born-digital archival records; computational literary studies.
• Strong motivation to work independently as well as with others within a diverse, interdisciplinary environment.
• Working proficiency in English and French; Italian is a plus.
• Self-discipline and creative thinking.
Collaborative environment and ambitious team
Application and Contact
• Academic CV
• Letter of motivation, explaining how you fit the candidate profile
• One writing sample (publication, PhD chapter)
• Contact details of two references
Please merge all the documents together into one PDF file and name the file as follows: yourSurname_BitPhil_postdoc.pdf (e.g. Spadini_BitPhil_postdoc.pdf).
Application deadline: 30 November 2026.
Interview dates: between 7 and 12 January 2027.
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## Research focus
The Bit Philology project studies born-digital materials in literary archives, with a focus on Swiss collections in French and Italian. As a significant portion of contemporary literature is created digitally, literary archives increasingly include born-digital documents-posing new challenges for their study. The project seeks to develop methods for cataloguing these archives, create prototypes for scholarly editions, and explore authors' creative processes through digital materials. It also aims to train future researchers and advance practices in textual scholarship and digital humanities. The project team is currently composed of two PhD students and a research associate in addition to the PI.
The postdoctoral researcher will work with born-digital archives of writers from Swiss collections dating from the 1980s to the early 2000s (Swiss Literary Archives, Centre des littératures en Suisse romande, Archivio Prezzolini). The postdoctoral researcher can develop their own research project, focusing on one or more authors and/or works. One possible research topic is the relationship between paper and digital documents in hybrid archives. In many cases, libraries and archives acquire digital content as part of a paper donation and these different sources should be studied together.

Sviluppa la tua linea di ricerca e partecipa alle attività del progetto. Ciò include
• lavorare negli archivi;
• chiarire i diritti e le potenziali questioni etiche;

• pubblicare e presentare il tuo lavoro a livello locale e internazionale;
• contribuire all'organizzazione di eventi accademici;

Profilo del candidato
Dottorato di ricerca in studi testuali (filologia, critica testuale, edizione scientifica, critica genetica), studi letterari o digital humanities.
• Esperienza pregressa nel lavoro con gli archivi.
• Esperienza pregressa o forte interesse per la letteratura svizzera francese contemporanea e/o la letteratura italiana; documenti d'archivio nativi digitali; studi letterari computazionali.
• Forte motivazione a lavorare in modo indipendente così come con altre persone in un ambiente diversificato e interdisciplinare.
• Buona padronanza dell'inglese e del francese; l'italiano costituisce un vantaggio.

Scadenza per la candidatura: 30 novembre 2026.
Date dei colloqui: tra il 7 e il 12 gennaio 2027.

Per te e per la società.

Ambito di ricerca
Il progetto Bit Philology studia i materiali nativi digitali negli archivi letterari, con particolare attenzione alle collezioni svizzere in francese e italiano. Poiché una parte significativa della letteratura contemporanea viene creata in formato digitale, gli archivi letterari includono sempre più documenti nativi digitali, ponendo nuove sfide per il loro studio. Il progetto mira a sviluppare metodi per la catalogazione di questi archivi, creare prototipi di edizioni scientifiche ed esplorare i processi creativi degli autori attraverso i materiali digitali. Mira inoltre a formare i futuri ricercatori e a far progredire le pratiche di filologia testuale e delle discipline umanistiche digitali. Il gruppo di progetto è attualmente composto da due dottorandi e da un ricercatore associato, oltre al PI.
Il ricercatore post-dottorale lavorerà con archivi nativi digitali di scrittori provenienti da collezioni svizzere, risalenti dagli anni Ottanta ai primi anni Duemila (Swiss Literary Archives, Centre des littératures en Suisse romande, Archivio Prezzolini). Il ricercatore post-dottorale potrà sviluppare il proprio progetto di ricerca, concentrandosi su uno o più autori e/o opere. Un possibile tema di ricerca è il rapporto tra i documenti cartacei e digitali negli archivi ibridi. ## Research focus
The Bit Philology project studies born-digital materials in literary archives, with a focus on Swiss collections in French and Italian. As a significant portion of contemporary literature is created digitally, literary archives increasingly include born-digital documents-posing new challenges for their study. The project seeks to develop methods for cataloguing these archives, create prototypes for scholarly editions, and explore authors' creative processes through digital materials. It also aims to train future researchers and advance practices in textual scholarship and digital humanities. The project team is currently composed of two PhD students and a research associate in addition to the PI.
The postdoctoral researcher will work with born-digital archives of writers from Swiss collections dating from the 1980s to the early 2000s (Swiss Literary Archives, Centre des littératures en Suisse romande, Archivio Prezzolini). The postdoctoral researcher can develop their own research project, focusing on one or more authors and/or works. One possible research topic is the relationship between paper and digital documents in hybrid archives. In many cases, libraries and archives acquire digital content as part of a paper donation and these different sources should be studied together.

Ihre Aufgaben und unser Angebot
Entwickeln Sie Ihre Forschungslinie weiter und beteiligen Sie sich an den Projektaktivitäten. Dazu gehören
• die Arbeit in Archiven;
• die Klärung von Rechten und potenziellen ethischen Fragen;
• die Kommunikation mit Archivarinnen und Archivaren sowie Autorinnen/Autoren bzw. Rechteinhaberinnen/Rechteinhabern;
• die Arbeit mit älterer Hardware und Software unter Einsatz digitalforensischer Methoden;
• die Untersuchung des Schreibprozesses von Autorinnen und Autoren über verschiedene Medien hinweg;
• die Untersuchung von Archivmaterialien wie unveröffentlichten Texten und Entwürfen für Publikationen;
• die Veröffentlichung und Präsentation Ihrer Arbeit auf lokaler und internationaler Ebene;
• die Mitwirkung an der Organisation wissenschaftlicher Veranstaltungen;
• die Zusammenarbeit mit dem restlichen Team.
Die Teilnahme an der Lehre ist optional. Das Startdatum ist März 2027, wobei ein späterer Start ebenfalls möglich ist.
Was wir bieten
• Ein dynamisches und kollaboratives Forschungsumfeld in der Einheit für Digital Humanities.
• Vereinbarkeit von Berufs- und Privatleben durch flexible Arbeitszeitmodelle.
• Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten in allen Bereichen des Projekts und verwandten Fachgebieten.
• Gehalt gemäß den SNSF-Reglementen.

Kandidatenprofil
Promotion in Textwissenschaft (Philologie, Textkritik, wissenschaftliches Edieren, genetische Kritik) oder Literaturwissenschaft oder Digital Humanities.
• Frühere Erfahrung in der Arbeit mit Archiven.
• Frühere Erfahrung oder starkes Interesse an zeitgenössischer schweizerischer französisch- und/oder italienischsprachiger Literatur; an digital entstandenen Archivunterlagen; an computergestützter Literaturwissenschaft.
• Starke Motivation, sowohl selbstständig als auch mit anderen in einem vielfältigen, interdisziplinären Umfeld zu arbeiten.
• Gute Arbeitskenntnisse in Englisch und Französisch; Italienisch ist von Vorteil.
• Selbstdisziplin und kreatives Denken.
Kooperatives Umfeld und ambitioniertes Team

Interviewtermine: zwischen dem 7. und 12. Januar 2027.

Für sich selbst und für die Gesellschaft.

Forschungsschwerpunkt
Das Projekt Bit Philology untersucht originär digitale Materialien in Literaturarchiven mit einem Schwerpunkt auf Schweizer Sammlungen in französischer und italienischer Sprache. Da ein erheblicher Teil der zeitgenössischen Literatur digital erstellt wird, umfassen Literaturarchive zunehmend originär digitale Dokumente, die neue Herausforderungen für ihre Erforschung mit sich bringen. Das Projekt zielt darauf ab, Methoden zur Katalogisierung dieser Archive zu entwickeln, Prototypen für wissenschaftliche Editionen zu erstellen und die kreativen Prozesse von Autorinnen und Autoren anhand digitaler Materialien zu erforschen. Außerdem sollen künftige Forschende ausgebildet und Praktiken der Textphilologie und der Digital Humanities weiterentwickelt werden. Das Projektteam besteht derzeit neben der PI aus zwei Doktorierenden und einer wissenschaftlichen Assistenz.
Sie arbeiten mit originär digitalen Archiven von Schriftstellerinnen und Schriftstellern aus Schweizer Sammlungen, die aus der Zeit von den 1980er-Jahren bis zu den frühen 2000er-Jahren stammen (Swiss Literary Archives, Centre des littératures en Suisse romande, Archivio Prezzolini). In vielen Fällen erwerben Bibliotheken und Archive digitale Inhalte als Teil einer Schenkung von Papiermaterialien, und diese unterschiedlichen Quellen sollten gemeinsam untersucht werden.

Pour vous-même et pour la société.

Axe de recherche
Le projet Bit Philology étudie des documents nativement numériques dans des archives littéraires, en se concentrant sur les collections suisses en français et en italien. Comme une part importante de la littérature contemporaine est créée sous forme numérique, les archives littéraires comprennent de plus en plus de documents nativement numériques, ce qui pose de nouveaux défis pour leur étude. Le projet vise à développer des méthodes de catalogage de ces archives, à créer des prototypes d’éditions savantes et à explorer les processus créatifs des auteurs à travers des documents numériques. Il vise également à former les futurs chercheurs et à faire progresser les pratiques en matière de philologie textuelle et d’humanités numériques. L’équipe du projet se compose actuellement de deux doctorants et d’un collaborateur scientifique, en plus de la personne responsable du projet.
La personne postdoctorante travaillera avec des archives nativement numériques d’écrivains issues de collections suisses datant des années 1980 au début des années 2000 (Swiss Literary Archives, Centre des littératures en Suisse romande, Archivio Prezzolini). La personne postdoctorante pourra développer son propre projet de recherche, en se concentrant sur un ou plusieurs auteurs et/ou œuvres. Un sujet de recherche possible est la relation entre les documents papier et numériques dans les archives hybrides. Dans de nombreux cas, les bibliothèques et les archives acquièrent du contenu numérique dans le cadre d’un don de documents papier, et ces différentes sources devraient être étudiées conjointement.

jobs.description:
UniBE is prestigious.
With us, you benefit from the excellent reputation of a long-standing institution all around the world.

## Requirements and Appointment
• PhD degree in physics, astronomy, or a similar discipline.
• Experience with astronomical instrumentation, preferably also in spectropolarimetry, optical design, or integral field imaging.
• Experience in programming with Python, further programming languages are considered an asset. Knowledge of Code V or Zemax is beneficial.
• Knowledge of ground- and space-based solar or stellar observations.
• Experience with project management and reviews (PDR/CDR).
• Teamplayer who likes to work with other group members and students.
The successful candidate will be expected to start in Bern after March 1, 2027, upon mutual agreement.
• Postdoc positions are initially budgeted for 2 years with annual contracts, with possibility for extension.
• Senior research assistant positions are renewed annually upon satisfactory performance.
The hiring level will be determined according to the candidate's previous experience and preferences. Senior candidates will be asked to manage the instrumentation group and further instrumentation projects and will be able to expand their teaching portfolio, with the prospect of becoming the deputy leader for the whole research group, and to qualify for a future permanent position in the institute.

## Information
The deadline for applications is November 29, 2026 via email to L. Kleint, containing (as one pdf file):
• CV
• a list of publications
• motivation letter for this specific position, addressing the requirements above.
• max. 2-page research statement describing past research and ideas for future research that would fit with our project.
• the names of 3 references that can be contacted.
Salary is based on the regulations of the University of Bern and your experience, starting at 91/103/121 (Early Postdoc / Advanced Postdoc / Senior Research Assistant) kCHF/year.
An equal opportunity environment is important to us, and we welcome applicants from groups that are traditionally underrepresented in physics and astronomy. We will be particularly pleased to receive applications from women for the advertised position.
Central location in the heart of Bern
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## About the position
The Space Weather group of the Astronomical Institute, University of Bern invites applications for a Postdoc or Senior Research Assistant (80-100%) to work on astronomical instrumentation.
The University of Bern hosts many domains of astronomy, from solar physics, to exoplanets, and satellite observations. The successful candidate will work in the space weather group, which focuses on understanding solar and stellar flares. This position is initially part of an ERC project with the goal of building a unique instrument to measure the full visible spectrum of flares. The first stellar prototype is already installed at the University's own observatory in Zimmerwald (80 cm telescope). The solar instrument version is in the design phase and planned to be used as a guest instrument. The goal of this position is to contribute to the design, review, and commissioning as part of our instrumentation team. The selected candidate will also have the opportunity to be involved in our adaptive optics project and further scientific work.
We are looking for highly motivated candidates with experience in astronomical instrumentation, in particular optics, instrument design, and spectrographs. You will be part of a research group of >10 people that combines instrumentation, machine learning, observations and models to answer questions such as "When and where will a flare occur? What are the origins and mechanisms of solar flares and stellar superflares?". This position includes management duties for documentation, reviews, and our optics lab.

• Esperienza con strumentazione astronomica, preferibilmente anche in spettropolarimetria, progettazione ottica, o imaging a campo integrale.
