jobs.description:
UniBE is interconnected.
With us, you're part of an international community and benefit from interdisciplinary collaboration.

## Your tasks
In close collaboration with other groups and project members, you will:
• Lead the development of a scalable, cloud-based platform integrating hydrological climate impact modelling workflows into a unified environment.
• Design and implement a modular platform architecture that enables users to configure, execute, monitor, and visualize hydrological simulations for different regions and applications.
• Containerize software components (e.g., using Docker) and deploy them on distributed cloud infrastructure.
• Implement workflow orchestration mechanisms to enable automated, parallel, and reproducible execution of modelling workflows.
• Develop a web-based user interface and programmatic APIs to provide intuitive access to the platform and facilitate integration with external tools and services.
• Implement mechanisms for data and workflow versioning, provenance tracking, user management, and access control to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and collaboration.
• Contribute to the development of a scalable data provisioning service, including data collection and integration, on-demand data extraction through web services, and automated data quality control.
• Collaborate closely with hydrologists, climate scientists, and data scientists to translate scientific requirements into robust and user-friendly software solutions.

## Your profile
• A degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
• Strong software engineering skills and experience developing complex software applications.
• Experience with cloud-based architectures, containerization (e.g., Docker), and distributed computing environments.
• Experience developing web applications and REST APIs.
• Familiarity with workflow orchestration, data management, and versioning systems.
• Experience with data processing and handling large scientific datasets is an asset.
• Interest in scientific applications, particularly hydrology, climate science, or environmental sciences.
• Ability to work independently, take initiative, and contribute to a collaborative interdisciplinary research environment.
• Excellent written and spoken English.
International reputation
Application and Contact
Please submit your application as a single PDF file, including:

jobs.description:
UniBE is ambitious.
With us, you deliver top performance and test your skills against the best.

## Your tasks
In close collaboration with other groups and project members, you will:
• Set up and compare process-based hydrological model structures using flexible, modular hydrological modelling frameworks.
• Implement new hydrological processes and functionalities in these frameworks where needed.
• Develop Python-based workflows to automate model setup across different catchments in Europe.
• Run large ensembles of simulations on computing clusters and evaluate model performance for mean, high and low flows, as well as key hydrological processes.
• Quantify and attribute sources of uncertainty throughout the climate impact assessment modelling chain.
• Collaborate on improving hydrological model calibration and training strategies, and on identifying region- and application-specific workflows for floods, droughts, and water availability.
• Publish your results in scientific journals and present them at international conferences.
• Train young colleagues (MSc students, PhD students) and occasionally contribute to teaching

## Your profile
• PhD in hydrology, environmental sciences, engineering, climate sciences, statistics or a closely related field with a strong focus on quantitative and numeric methods.
• Strong background in geoscientific modelling, ideally with process-based hydrologic models; experience with flexible modelling frameworks and hybrid-AI methods is an asset.
• Strong programming skills in Python and experience with the analysis of hydrological and/or climate datasets.
• Ease in handling and integrating data from different sources, including geospatial data and geodata formats.
• Experience or a strong interest in uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis and ensemble-based approaches.
• Excellent scientific writing and communication skills in English, with the ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary team.
International reputation
Application and Contact
Please submit your application as a single PDF file, including:
• A short letter of motivation outlining your interest in the position and relevant experience.
• A CV (maximum 2 pages, excluding the publication list), including your ORCID number.
• A short document (maximum 1 page) describing your relevant experience in developing, calibrating and applying models; performing uncertainty quantification; and software development or programming. Please also list up to three relevant scientific publications and briefly describe your personal contribution to each.
• Copies of your degree certificates and academic transcripts.
Please submit your application by January 8, 2027
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## What we offer
You will work in the project “HydroImpact: Hydrological Climate Impact Platform” (https://hydroimpact.org/), which is funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) and Innosuisse through the BRIDGE Discovery funding scheme. HydroImpact aims to make targeted hydrological climate impact assessments widely accessible to practitioners and engineers in Europe by building a cloud-based platform that integrates state-of-the-art AI and hydrological modelling tools and follows a stakeholder co-design process.
You will be part of the Hydrology Group at the Institute of Geography of the University of Bern, a small and collaborative team working on hydrological modelling and climate change impacts, among other topics. The group is closely connected to the Oeschger Centre for Climate Change Research (OCCR) and offers opportunities to engage with a wide range of hydrological methods and research approaches.
The project involves close collaboration with researchers at WSL and ETH Zurich (Prof. Manuela Brunner) and the Swiss Data Science Center (SDSC) at EPFL (Prof. Mathieu Salzmann). This interdisciplinary environment offers opportunities for scientific exchange, collaboration and professional development. You will be supervised by Dr. Pascal Horton, who will coordinate the work in close collaboration with the project partners.

UniBE è ambizioso.
Con noi, si offre le migliori prestazioni e testare le vostre abilità contro il meglio.

## I tuoi compiti
In stretta collaborazione con altri gruppi e membri del progetto, si:
• Configurare e confrontare le strutture di modelli idrologici a base di processo utilizzando strutture di modellazione idrologica flessibili e modulari.
• Implementare nuovi processi idrologici e funzionalità in questi quadri dove necessario.
• Sviluppare flussi di lavoro basati su Python per automatizzare la configurazione del modello in diverse catture in Europa.
• Eseguire grandi gruppi di simulazioni su cluster di calcolo e valutare le prestazioni del modello per flussi medi, alti e bassi, così come i processi idrologici chiave.
• Quantifica e attribuisci fonti di incertezza in tutta la catena di modellizzazione della valutazione dell'impatto climatico.
• Collaborate al miglioramento delle strategie di calibrazione e formazione del modello idrologico e all'individuazione dei flussi di lavoro specifici per regione e applicazione per inondazioni, siccità e disponibilità dell'acqua.
• Pubblica i tuoi risultati in riviste scientifiche e presentali a conferenze internazionali.
• Formare giovani colleghi (studenti MSc, dottorandi) e occasionalmente contribuire all'insegnamento

## Il tuo profilo
• PhD in idrologia, scienze ambientali, ingegneria, scienze del clima, statistiche o un campo strettamente correlato con una forte attenzione ai metodi quantitativi e numerici.
• Forte sfondo nella modellazione geoscientifica, idealmente con modelli idrologici basati sul processo; l'esperienza con strutture modellanti flessibili e metodi ibridi-AI è un bene.
• Forte capacità di programmazione in Python e esperienza con l'analisi di dataset idrologici e/o climatici.
• Facilita la gestione e l'integrazione dei dati da diverse fonti, inclusi i dati geospaziali e i formati geodati.
• Esperienza o un forte interesse per la quantificazione dell'incertezza, l'analisi della sensibilità e gli approcci basati su ensemble.
• Eccellente capacità di scrittura e comunicazione scientifica in inglese, con la capacità di lavorare in modo indipendente e collaborativo in un team interdisciplinare.

Si prega di inviare la domanda come un singolo file PDF, tra cui:
• Una breve lettera di motivazione che sottolinea il vostro interesse per la posizione e l'esperienza rilevante.
• Un CV (massimo 2 pagine, escluso l'elenco di pubblicazione), incluso il numero ORCID.
• Un breve documento (massimo 1 pagina) che descrive la vostra esperienza rilevante nello sviluppo, nella calibrazione e nell'applicazione dei modelli; nella quantificazione dell'incertezza e nello sviluppo o nella programmazione del software. Si prega inoltre di elencare fino a tre pubblicazioni scientifiche pertinenti e descrivere brevemente il vostro contributo personale a ciascuno.
• Copie dei certificati di laurea e trascrizioni accademiche.
Invia la tua richiesta entro il 8 gennaio 2027
Con noi, crei valore.
Per te e per la società.

## Cosa offriamo
Lavorerai nel progetto “HydroImpact: Hydrological Climate Impact Platform” (https://hydroimpact.org/), finanziato dalla Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) e Innosuisse attraverso lo schema di finanziamento BRIDGE Discovery. HydroImpact mira a rendere le valutazioni di impatto ambientale mirate ampiamente accessibili ai professionisti e agli ingegneri in Europa costruendo una piattaforma cloud-based che integra strumenti di modellazione idrologica e AI all'avanguardia e segue un processo di co-design degli stakeholder.
Sarete parte del Gruppo Hydrology presso l'Istituto di Geografia dell'Università di Berna, un piccolo e collaborativo team che si occupa di modellazione idrologica e impatto sui cambiamenti climatici, tra gli altri temi. Il gruppo è strettamente connesso al Centro Oeschger per la Ricerca sul Cambiamento Climatico (OCCR) e offre opportunità di impegnarsi con una vasta gamma di metodi idrologici e approcci di ricerca.
Il progetto prevede una stretta collaborazione con i ricercatori della WSL e dell'ETH di Zurigo (Prof. Manuela Brunner) e dello Swiss Data Science Center (SDSC) dell'EPFL (Prof. Mathieu Salzmann). Questo ambiente interdisciplinare offre opportunità di scambio scientifico, collaborazione e sviluppo professionale. Sarà supervisionato dal Dr. Pascal Horton, che coordinerà il lavoro in stretta collaborazione con i partner del progetto.

jobs.description:
UniBE is interconnected.
With us, you're part of an international community and benefit from interdisciplinary collaboration.

## Focus
The main focus of the PostDoc position will be on orbit and gravity field recovery using the GNSS data of the zenith-looking antennas of the Spire Global satellite constellation and further scientific LEO missions. Optimum combination schemes shall be developed to improve the recovery of the very long-wavelength part of the Earth's time-variable gravity field from normal equations that are based on kinematic positions stemming from satellites at different altitudes and providing GNSS data of inhomogeneous quality.
The candidate should start working in Bern on February 01, 2027.
The PostDoc project is scheduled for two years. The salary follows the guidelines of the Swiss National Science Foundation for PostDoc positions.

## Education
The candidate is expected to have successfully completed a Ph.D. thesis in astronomy, geodesy, physics, aerospace engineering, or a related discipline. Experience in orbit and gravity field determination from satellite data is an advantage. Background in computer science (coding in Fortran, C++, Python or Perl) is not a requirement, but beneficial for working on this project. The candidate should be able to speak and write English fluently.
• Strong research infrastructure and international network

• Prof. Dr. Adrian Jäggi
• Astronomical Institute
• University of Bern
• Sidlerstrasse 5
• CH-3012 Bern

• With us, you create value.
• For yourself and for society.

## Description
• The group “Space Geodesy” of the Astronomical Institute of the University of Bern (AIUB) offers the position for a PostDoc.
• The focus will be on the determination of time-variable Earth's gravity fields from real GNSS data of CubeSat constellations and scientific Low Earth Orbiting (LEO) satellite missions.
Today, more and more commercial satellites equipped with dual-frequency GNSS receivers are launched, e.g., from Spire Global, a satellite-powered data company that uses a large, distribut-ed constellation of multi-payload nano-satellites. These satellites have the potential to provide high-temporal-resolution measurements through entire CubeSat constellations, which can miti-gate existing data gaps and improve Earth science phenomena by sustained observations with increased spatial and temporal resolution.

UniBE ist prestigeträchtig.
Bei uns profitieren Sie vom exzellenten Ruf einer langjährigen Institution auf der ganzen Welt.

## Wir schauen
für einen motivierten Doktoranden mit einem abgeschlossenen MSc in Biologie (oder gleichwertig) mit einem starken Interesse an Einzelzellgenomik, Pflanzenentwicklung und Sukkulentenbiologie und idealerweise Erfahrung mit Pflanzenmolekularbiologie, Mikroskopie und Pflanzengenetik. Eine offene, kooperative Denkweise für die Arbeit in unserem dynamischen, unterstützenden Team wird erwartet.

## Beantragt
Bitte senden Sie ein einzelnes PDF mit Motivationsschreiben, Lebenslauf und Namen von mindestens zwei Schiedsrichtern an heike.lindner@unibe.ch. Das Startdatum der Position ist der 1. April 2027 oder nach Vereinbarung. Wir werden mit der Prüfung der Anträge am 21. Dezember 2026 beginnen.
Teamorientierte Arbeit
• Mit uns schaffen Sie Werte.
• Für dich und für die Gesellschaft.

## Über uns
Die Gruppe „Functional Anatomy of Succulents ist am Institut für Pflanzenwissenschaften der Universität Bern angesiedelt und freut sich über Bewerbungen für eine vollfinanzierte Doktorandenstelle (4 Jahre). Unsere Gruppe untersucht die Entwicklung der Sukkulenten Blattanatomie, um zu verstehen, wie diese spezialisierte Anatomie den wassereffizientesten Modus der Photosynthese, den Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM), unterstützt. Wir kombinieren Einzelzellgenomik, Molekularbiologie, Biotechnologie, Bildgebung, Genetik und Gasaustauschphysiologie, um das Zusammenspiel zwischen Blattanatomie und Photosynthese in Kalanchoë laxiflora zu verstehen (weitere Details zu unserer Gruppe finden Sie unter https://www.ips.unibe.ch/research/cam/index eng.html).
Gefördert wird das Projekt vom Schweizerischen Nationalfonds (SNF). Wir haben die saftige CAM-Pflanze Kalanchoë laxiflora als experimentelles Modellsystem im Labor etabliert (Cheng, Lindner et al., 2026). In diesem Projekt wollen wir die Single-Cell-Multi-Omics-, Imaging- und Entwicklungsgenetik nutzen, um Module zu identifizieren, die die Entwicklung der saftigen Blattanatomie regulieren, um zu analysieren, wie diese spezialisierte Blattanatomie die CAM-Photosynthese unterstützt.
Wir bieten eine lebendige und integrative Forschungsumgebung, die grundlegende Fragen der Pflanzenentwicklung und Physiologie von Gräsern und Sukkulenten beantworten möchte (siehe unser Laborleitbild: https://docs.google.com/document/d/19QScwNTy67 cAVnZQlZ- yuvM wYsK0T8dyPOD1OSyE/edit?tab=t.0)
Wir bieten eine hochmoderne Forschungsinfrastruktur am Institut für Pflanzenwissenschaften in Bern (http://www.ips.unibe.ch/) und sind auch dem Oeschger-Zentrum für Klimaforschung (www.oeschger.unibe.ch) angeschlossen.

pour un doctorant motivé ayant une maîtrise en biologie (ou l'équivalent) avec un vif intérêt pour la génomique monocellulaire, le développement végétal et la biologie succulente, et, idéalement, l'expérience en biologie moléculaire végétale, en microscopie et en génétique végétale. Veuillez envoyer un seul PDF comprenant une lettre de motivation, un CV et les noms d'au moins deux répondants à heike.lindner@unibe.ch. La date de début du poste sera le 1er avril 2027 ou à la date prévue. Nous commencerons à examiner les demandes le 21 décembre 2026.
Travaux axés sur l ' équipe

## À propos de nous
Le groupe d'anatomie fonctionnelle des succulents est accueilli à l'Institut des sciences des plantes de l'Université de Berne et accueille les candidatures pour un doctorat entièrement financé (4 ans). Notre groupe étudie le développement succulent de l'anatomie foliaire pour comprendre comment cette anatomie spécialisée soutient le mode le plus efficace d'utilisation de l'eau de la photosynthèse, Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM). Nous combinons la génomique monocellulaire, la biologie moléculaire, la biotechnologie, l'imagerie, la génétique et la physiologie de l'échange de gaz pour comprendre l'interaction entre l'anatomie des feuilles et la photosynthèse à Kalanchoë laxiflora (pour plus de détails sur notre groupe, voir https://www.ips.unibe.ch/research/cam/index eng.html).
Le projet est financé par la Fondation nationale suisse des sciences (SNSF). Nous avons établi la succulente plante CAM Kalanchoë laxiflora comme un modèle expérimental dans le laboratoire (Cheng, Lindner et al., 2026). Dans le cadre de ce projet, nous voulons utiliser la multiomique monocellulaire, l'imagerie et la génétique du développement pour identifier des modules qui régulent le développement succulent de l'anatomie foliaire pour disséquer comment cette anatomie foliaire spécialisée soutient la photosynthèse CAM.
Nous offrons un environnement de recherche dynamique et inclusif qui s'efforce de répondre aux questions fondamentales en matière de développement des plantes et de physiologie des graminées et des succulents (voir notre énoncé de mission de laboratoire : https://docs.google.com/document/d/19QScwNTy67 cAVnZQlZ- yuvM wYsK0T8dyPOD1OSyE/edit?tab=t.0)
Nous offrons une infrastructure de recherche de pointe à l'Institut des sciences des plantes de Berne (http://www.ips.unibe.ch/) et sommes également affiliés au Centre Oeschger pour la recherche sur les changements climatiques (www.oeschger.unibe.ch).

UniBE is prestigious.
With us, you benefit from the excellent reputation of a long-standing institution all around the world.

## You have:
• A university degree (MD, MSc or equivalent) in medicine, epidemiology, health sciences, or related fields
• A strong interest in child health and/or public health
• Experience in data analysis and statistical software such as R or Stata.
• Fluency in English and German. French or Italian are an asset.

## What we offer:
• You work in a motivated and competent research team
• We prepare you for a research career in a university (paediatrics, epidemiology or preventive medicine) or a public health institution
• The PhD counts as medical training (in Paediatrics or Public Health)
• We have a lively and international graduate school at the University of Bern
• Salary according to the Swiss National Science Foundation Salary Scales for PhD students
Period: PhD contract for 3 years, start as soon as possible
Supervisor: PD Dr. Fabiën Belle
Place: ISPM University of Bern, Switzerland
Collaborative environment and ambitious team
Application and Contact
If you are looking for an exciting position in a highly motivated interdisciplinary team, please send your CV with motivation letter to Dr. med. Maša Žarković and PD. Dr. Fabiën Belle by December 14, 2026.
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## About us:
The Institute of Social and Preventive Medicine (ISPM) of Bern performs research in a range of disciplines relevant to public health (www.ispm.unibe.ch). Groups cut across divisions, facilitating an interdisciplinary approach to research in the fields of clinical epidemiology, social and behavioural health, biostatistics, and international and environmental health. The ISPM is highly reputed for its expertise in the health of vulnerable groups including children. The Child and Adolescent Health Group, headed by Prof. Dr. med. Claudia Kuehni, conducts population-based and clinical studies in child health.
Childhood cancer survivors often face chronic health problems that resulted in late side effects of the cancer or its treatment. In Switzerland, we have an ongoing national cohort study, the Swiss Childhood Cancer Survivor Study (SCCSS, www.swiss-ccss.ch), which monitors health in survivors of childhood and adolescent cancer. While we have already studied specific late effects, we have not yet investigated the combined burden of health problems. In this PhD project you will group late-onset health effects of cancer treatments in children, including all types of health problems and grading severity according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE). Thus, you can assess the overall and excess burden of curative cancer therapy for the past decades and recently treated children. You will compare survivors' health to their siblings, identify predictors of severe toxicities, and compare results from Switzerland to international data. Your PhD will be the first worldwide that grades chronic health conditions in a national sample of children and adolescents, because previous studies were limited to adult survivors. By adopting an internationally standardized approach, you will contribute to improving survivorship care and stimulating ongoing and future national and international research on late consequences of cancer care in children.
You will be part of a dynamic and multidisciplinary team and work closely with clinicians, epidemiologists, data managers, and other PhD students. You will gain an in-depth understanding of epidemiological and biostatistical techniques, expand your (inter)national network, present your results at (inter)national conferences, and publish in peer-reviewed journals.

## Hai...

• Un forte interesse per la salute dei bambini e/o la salute pubblica
• Esperienza nell'analisi dei dati e software statistico come R o Stata.

## Cosa offriamo:

Se siete alla ricerca di una posizione emozionante in un team interdisciplinare altamente motivato, si prega di inviare il vostro CV con lettera di motivazione a info@swiss-ccs.ch, Dr. med. Maša Žarković (masa.zarkovic@unibe.ch) e PD. Dr. Fabiën Belle (fabien.belle@unibe.ch) entro il 14 dicembre 2026.
Con noi, crei valore.
Per te e per la società.

## Su di noi:
L'Istituto di Medicina Sociale e Preventiva (ISPM) di Berna svolge ricerche in una serie di discipline rilevanti per la salute pubblica (www.ispm.unibe.ch). I gruppi hanno tagliato le divisioni, facilitando un approccio interdisciplinare alla ricerca nel campo dell'epidemiologia clinica, della salute sociale e comportamentale, della biostatistica e della salute internazionale e ambientale. L'ISPM è molto apprezzato per la sua esperienza nella salute di gruppi vulnerabili, compresi i bambini. Il Gruppo di Salute Bambino e Adolescente, guidato dal Prof. Dottor Med. Claudia Kuehni, conduce studi clinici e basati sulla popolazione nella salute dei bambini.
I sopravvissuti al cancro dell'infanzia affrontano spesso problemi di salute cronici che hanno causato effetti collaterali tardivi del cancro o del suo trattamento. In Svizzera, abbiamo uno studio di coorte nazionale in corso, lo studio di sopravvivenza del cancro all'infanzia svizzero (SCCSS, www.swiss-ccs.ch), che monitora la salute nei sopravvissuti al cancro dell'infanzia e dell'adolescenza. Mentre abbiamo già studiato specifici effetti in ritardo, non abbiamo ancora indagato l'onere combinato dei problemi di salute. In questo progetto di PhD si raggruppano gli effetti di salute tardivi dei trattamenti per il cancro nei bambini, compresi tutti i tipi di problemi di salute e la gravità del grading secondo i criteri di terminologia comune per gli eventi avversi (CTCAE). Così, è possibile valutare l'onere generale ed eccesso di terapia curativa del cancro per gli ultimi decenni e bambini recentemente trattati. Confronterai la salute dei sopravvissuti ai loro fratelli, identificherai i predittori delle tossicità gravi e confronta i risultati dalla Svizzera ai dati internazionali. Il tuo dottorato sarà il primo in tutto il mondo che classifica le condizioni di salute croniche in un campione nazionale di bambini e adolescenti, perché gli studi precedenti erano limitati ai sopravvissuti adulti. Adottando un approccio standardizzato a livello internazionale, contribuirai a migliorare l'assistenza ai sopravvissuti e a stimolare la ricerca nazionale e internazionale in corso e futura sulle conseguenze tardive dell'assistenza al cancro nei bambini.
Sarai parte di un team dinamico e multidisciplinare e lavorerai a stretto contatto con medici, epidemiologi, responsabili dei dati e altri studenti del dottorato. Acquisrai una comprensione approfondita delle tecniche epidemiologiche e biostatistiche, espanderai la tua (inter) rete nazionale, presenterai i tuoi risultati alle conferenze nazionali (inter) e pubblicherai su riviste peer-reviewed.

The ISPM is highly reputed for its expertise in the health of vulnerable groups including children. The Child and Adolescent Health Group, headed by Prof. Dr. med. Claudia Kuehni, conducts population-based and clinical studies in child health.
Childhood cancer survivors often face chronic health problems that resulted in late side effects of the cancer or its treatment. In Switzerland, we have an ongoing national cohort study, the Swiss Childhood Cancer Survivor Study (SCCSS, www.swiss-ccss.ch), which monitors health in survivors of childhood and adolescent cancer. While we have already studied specific late effects, we have not yet investigated the combined burden of health problems. In this PhD project you will group late-onset health effects of cancer treatments in children, including all types of health problems and grading severity according to the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE). Thus, you can assess the overall and excess burden of curative cancer therapy for the past decades and recently treated children. You will compare survivors' health to their siblings, identify predictors of severe toxicities, and compare results from Switzerland to international data. Your PhD will be the first worldwide that grades chronic health conditions in a national sample of children and adolescents, because previous studies were limited to adult survivors. By adopting an internationally standardized approach, you will contribute to improving survivorship care and stimulating ongoing and future national and international research on late consequences of cancer care in children.
You will be part of a dynamic and multidisciplinary team and work closely with clinicians, epidemiologists, data managers, and other PhD students. You will gain an in-depth understanding of epidemiological and biostatistical techniques, expand your (inter)national network, present your results at (inter)national conferences, and publish in peer-reviewed journals.

Das Institut für Sozial- und Präventivmedizin (ISPM) in Bern forscht in verschiedenen für die öffentliche Gesundheit relevanten Disziplinen (www.ispm.unibe.ch). Gruppen schneiden über Abteilungen hinweg und erleichtern einen interdisziplinären Ansatz für die Forschung in den Bereichen klinische Epidemiologie, Sozial- und Verhaltensgesundheit, Biostatistik sowie internationale und Umweltgesundheit. Die ISPM ist bekannt für ihre Expertise in der Gesundheit von gefährdeten Gruppen, einschließlich Kindern. Die Child and Adolescent Health Group, geleitet von Prof. Dr. med. Claudia Kuehni führt bevölkerungsbasierte und klinische Studien zur Gesundheit von Kindern durch.
Krebsüberlebende im Kindesalter haben oft chronische Gesundheitsprobleme, die zu späten Nebenwirkungen des Krebses oder seiner Behandlung führten. In der Schweiz haben wir eine laufende nationale Kohortenstudie, die Swiss Childhood Cancer Survivor Study (SCCSS, www.swiss-ccss.ch), die die Gesundheit von Überlebenden von Kinder- und Jugendkrebs überwacht. Durch einen international standardisierten Ansatz tragen Sie dazu bei, die Überlebensbetreuung zu verbessern und die laufende und zukünftige nationale und internationale Forschung zu den Spätfolgen der Krebsbehandlung bei Kindern zu fördern.

## Vous avez :
• Diplôme universitaire (MD, maîtrise ou équivalent) en médecine, épidémiologie, sciences de la santé ou domaines connexes

Avec nous, vous créez de la valeur.
Pour vous et pour la société.

## À propos de nous :
L'Institut de médecine sociale et préventive (ISPM) de Berne effectue des recherches dans un éventail de disciplines intéressant la santé publique (www.ispm.unibe.ch). Les groupes se répartissent en plusieurs divisions, facilitant une approche interdisciplinaire de la recherche dans les domaines de l'épidémiologie clinique, de la santé sociale et comportementale, de la biostatistique et de la santé internationale et environnementale. L'ISPM est réputée pour son expertise en matière de santé des groupes vulnérables, y compris les enfants. Le Groupe de la santé des enfants et des adolescents, dirigé par le Prof. Docteur Med. Claudia Kuehni mène des études cliniques et démographiques sur la santé des enfants.
Les survivants du cancer de l'enfance sont souvent confrontés à des problèmes de santé chroniques qui ont entraîné des effets secondaires tardifs du cancer ou de son traitement. En Suisse, nous avons une étude de cohorte nationale en cours, l'Étude suisse sur le cancer de l'enfant (SCCSS, www.swiss-ccs.ch), qui surveille la santé des survivants du cancer de l'enfant et de l'adolescent. Bien que nous ayons déjà étudié certains effets tardifs, nous n'avons pas encore étudié le fardeau combiné des problèmes de santé. Dans le cadre de ce projet de doctorat, vous regrouperez les effets sur la santé des traitements contre le cancer chez les enfants, y compris tous les types de problèmes de santé et la sévérité du classement selon les critères terminologiques communs pour les événements indésirables. Ainsi, vous pouvez évaluer le fardeau global et excessif de la thérapie curative contre le cancer pour les dernières décennies et les enfants récemment traités. Vous comparerez la santé des survivants à leurs frères et sœurs, identifierez les prédicteurs de toxicités graves et comparerez les résultats de la Suisse aux données internationales. Votre doctorat sera le premier dans le monde à classer les maladies chroniques dans un échantillon national d'enfants et d'adolescents, car les études antérieures ont été limitées aux survivants adultes. En adoptant une approche normalisée à l'échelle internationale, vous contribuerez à améliorer les soins de survie et stimulerez la recherche nationale et internationale continue et future sur les conséquences tardives des soins contre le cancer chez les enfants.
Vous ferez partie d'une équipe dynamique et multidisciplinaire et travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec des cliniciens, des épidémiologistes, des gestionnaires de données et d'autres doctorants. Vous acquerrez une compréhension approfondie des techniques épidémiologiques et biostatistiques, élargirez votre réseau (inter)national, présenterez vos résultats à des conférences (inter)nationales et publierez dans des revues évaluées par des pairs.

• PhD in public health, epidemiology or a related life sciences field

jobs.description:
UniBE is interconnected.
With us, you're part of an international community and benefit from interdisciplinary collaboration.

## 
• Your profile
We are seeking talented candidates (max. 7 years post PhD, career breaks and alternative career paths will be taken into account) with a competitive research program in synthetic organic chemistry with a clear focus on Pharmaceutical Chemistry. Possible research topics include (but are not limited to): natural product synthesis, oligonucleotides, encoded libraries, peptide chemistry, medicinal chemistry including computer-aided drug design, and antibiotics. Alignment of the research with the strategic goals of the University of Bern (in particular sustainability, health and medicine) is important.
Teaching assignments comprise basic and advanced organic, pharmaceutical and medicinal chemistry including laboratory courses for students of chemistry, biochemistry, pharmacy within the Faculty of Science.
In line with its commitment to fostering an inclusive academic environment, the University of Bern actively seeks to increase the proportion of women and other underrepresented groups in leadership positions. We warmly encourage such candidates to apply. As a signatory of the DORA declaration and ARRA agreement, the University of Bern applies their principles to ensure fair and transparent recruitment.

jobs.description:
UniBE is prestigious.
With us, you benefit from the excellent reputation of a long-standing institution all around the world.

## Your responsibilities
• Doctoral research with Jean-Michel Benkert (up to two positions).
• You will join a group of PhD students, postdocs, and faculty who exchange ideas in reading groups, seminars, and research discussions.
• We provide close supervision and support careers in academic research and public or private institutions.
• Successful candidates participate in the group's teaching and research activities and normally attend first-year doctoral courses at the Study Center Gerzensee.

## Your profile
• Applicants must hold, or expect to complete before starting, a master's degree in economics or another relevant discipline, with an excellent academic record.
• Beyond economics, we welcome backgrounds including mathematics, physics, computer science, psychology, sociology, and business.
• We value research potential, strong analytical skills, and sufficient quantitative preparation for rigorous doctoral coursework in economics.
• Proficiency in English is required.
• We welcome applications from qualified candidates of all backgrounds.
International reputation
Application and Contact
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until the positions are filled. Full application instructions and cover-letter guidance:
Please send a CV, a cover letter (maximum one page), your master's thesis or another research sample, and academic transcripts directly to Jean-Michel Benkert (jean-michel.benkert@unibe.ch). Please arrange for one academic recommendation letter to be sent to the same address. Questions are welcome at this address.
We are interested in your thinking. Please write your cover letter yourself, using a concrete question or experience to introduce your research interests and yourself. AI tools may assist with language correction, but please do not submit an AI-generated letter.
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## About the positions
One position is funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) through the project "When Do Expectations Bite? Micro-Founding Reference-Dependent Preferences." The project combines theory and experiments to study how expectations shape preferences and economic decisions. The second position is departmentally funded and offers scope for broader research in microeconomics, including behavioral economics, mechanism design, organizational economics, and industrial organization.

jobs.description:
UniBE is interconnected.
With us, you're part of an international community and benefit from interdisciplinary collaboration.

## Description of the project and position
This PhD project investigates how high-fat diet exposure disrupts the small intestinal barrier and contributes to the development of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Using advanced murine models, human intestinal organoids, and intestinal endothelial cell cultures, the project aims to unravel the molecular mechanisms underlying diet-induced barrier dysfunction, with a particular focus on β-adrenergic signaling and epithelial and endothelial permeability. Combining in vivo experiments with functional barrier assays, imaging, and molecular analyses, the project will explore how dietary fat alters intestinal barrier integrity and function and may identify novel therapeutic targets to prevent gut barrier dysfunction and its contribution to metabolic and liver disease.
Studies will be conducted in the Department of BioMedical Research (DBMR), in the research laboratories of the Gastroenterology/Mucosal Immunology division. We offer a highly interdisciplinary research environment dedicated to the study of mucosal immunology, microbiota, inflammation, and cancer development, involving human work, animal studies, and computational biology, besides close supervision and a great team spirit.
Payment is based on the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF)'s funding regulations for PhD students.

## Requirements
Candidates hold a M. Sc. in Immunology, Microbiology, Molecular Biology, Biotechnology, Animal Science, or any related fields in biological sciences. As the work involves animal experiments under gnotobiotic conditions, a general interest in such techniques is required. Excellent command of English language (oral and written) is a requirement.
Individual career support

• cover letter

• copies of academic degrees and transcripts of records
• contact information of 1-2 previous advisors for reference
• list of publications (do not include your publications in the pdf file).
The application deadline is January 17, 2027.
With us, you create value.
For yourself and for society.

## Description
The Wiest group at the Division of Gastroenterology and Mucosal Immunology at the Department for BioMedical Research at the University of Bern is looking for a PhD student to work on a project on High-fat-diet (HFD) induced disruption of instestinal barriers.
Our group is interested in the mechanisms leading to intestinal barrier breakage, pathological bacterial translocation in obesity and gut-liver interactions in chronic liver disease, using a wide range of techniques and model systems ranging from mouse models, via intestinal organoid cultures to human cohorts (Castillo et al, 2026, PMID: 42521089; Wyss et al, 2026, PMID: 41999240).
The work will be conducted in close collaboration with the group of Prof. Stephanie Ganal-Vonarburg, who investigates the impact of dietary and microbial signals on intestinal and immune development in early life.

## Descrizione del progetto e della posizione
Questo progetto PhD indaga su come l'esposizione di dieta ricca di grassi interrompe la piccola barriera intestinale e contribuisce allo sviluppo della malattia del fegato steatotico associata alla disfunzione metabolica (MASLD). Utilizzando modelli murini avanzati, organoidi intestinali umani e culture delle cellule endoteliali intestinali, il progetto mira a svelare i meccanismi molecolari sottostanti disfunzione della barriera indotta dalla dieta, con particolare attenzione alla segnalazione β-adrenergica e alla permeabilità epiteliale ed endoteliale. Combinando esperimenti in vivo con analisi funzionali della barriera, immagini e analisi molecolari, il progetto esplorerà come il grasso alimentare altera l'integrità e la funzione della barriera intestinale e può identificare nuovi obiettivi terapeutici per prevenire la disfunzione della barriera intestinale e il suo contributo alla malattia metabolica e del fegato.
Gli studi saranno condotti presso il Dipartimento di BioMedical Research (DBMR), nei laboratori di ricerca della divisione Gastroenterologia/Mucosal Immunology. Offriamo un ambiente di ricerca altamente interdisciplinare dedicato allo studio di immunologia mucosa, microbiota, infiammazione e sviluppo del cancro, coinvolgendo il lavoro umano, gli studi sugli animali e la biologia computazionale, oltre a una stretta supervisione e un grande spirito di squadra.
Il pagamento si basa sulle norme di finanziamento della Fondazione nazionale svizzera per gli studenti di dottorato.

Il gruppo Wiest della Divisione Gastroenterologia e Immunologia Mucosale presso il Dipartimento per la Ricerca Biomedicale dell'Università di Berna sta cercando uno studente di dottorato per lavorare su un progetto su High-fat-diet (HFD) indotto disordini di barriere instestinali.
Il nostro gruppo è interessato ai meccanismi che portano alla rottura della barriera intestinale, alla traslocazione batterica patologica nelle interazioni tra obesità e gut-liver nella malattia epatica cronica, utilizzando una vasta gamma di tecniche e sistemi di modelli che vanno dai modelli del mouse, attraverso culture organoidi intestinali alle coorte umane (Castillo et al, 2026, PMID: 42521089; Wysss et al, 2026, PMID: 41999240).
Il lavoro sarà svolto in stretta collaborazione con il gruppo del Prof. Stephanie Ganal-Vonarburg, che indaga l'impatto dei segnali dietetici e microbici sullo sviluppo intestinale e immunitario nella prima vita.

Bei uns sind Sie Teil einer internationalen Gemeinschaft und profitieren von interdisziplinärer Zusammenarbeit.

## Beschreibung des Projekts und Position
Dieses PhD-Projekt untersucht, wie fettreiche Ernährung die kleine Darmbarriere stört und zur Entwicklung einer metabolischen Dysfunktion-assoziierten steatotischen Lebererkrankung (MASLD) beiträgt. Mit fortschrittlichen Mausmodellen, menschlichen Darmorganoiden und intestinalen endothelialen Zellkulturen zielt das Projekt darauf ab, die molekularen Mechanismen zu entschlüsseln, die der ernährungsbedingten Barrierefunktion zugrunde liegen, wobei ein besonderer Schwerpunkt auf der β-adrenergen Signalisierung und der epithelialen und endothelialen Permeabilität liegt. Durch die Kombination von In-vivo-Experimenten mit funktionellen Barriere-Assays, Bildgebung und molekularen Analysen wird das Projekt untersuchen, wie Nahrungsfett die Integrität und Funktion der Darmbarriere verändert und neue therapeutische Ziele identifizieren kann, um eine Darmbarrierefunktionsstörung und ihren Beitrag zu Stoffwechsel- und Lebererkrankungen zu verhindern.
Studien werden in der Abteilung für biomedizinische Forschung (DBMR) und in den Forschungslabors der Abteilung Gastroenterologie/Mukosale Immunologie durchgeführt. Wir bieten ein hoch interdisziplinäres Forschungsumfeld, das sich dem Studium der Schleimhautimmunologie, der Mikrobiota, der Entzündung und der Krebsentwicklung widmet und menschliche Arbeit, Tierstudien und Computerbiologie umfasst, neben einer engen Überwachung und einem großartigen Teamgeist.
Die Zahlung erfolgt auf der Grundlage der Förderregelungen des Schweizerischen Nationalfonds (SNF) für Doktoranden.

## Anforderungen
Die Kandidaten haben einen M. Sc. in Immunologie, Mikrobiologie, Molekularbiologie, Biotechnologie, Tierwissenschaften oder verwandten Bereichen in den Biowissenschaften. Da die Arbeit Tierversuche unter gnotobiotischen Bedingungen beinhaltet, ist ein allgemeines Interesse an solchen Techniken erforderlich. Ausgezeichnete Beherrschung der englischen Sprache (mündlich und schriftlich) ist eine Voraussetzung.
Individuelle Karriereunterstützung

Bitte senden Sie Ihre Bewerbung in einer einzigen PDF-Datei mit dem Namen „application firstname.lastname“, die „PhD-Position“ im E-Mail-Betreff angibt.
Die Datei sollte Folgendes enthalten:
• Begleitschreiben
• Lebenslauf (es muss das Datumsformat mm/JJJJ haben)
• Kopien von akademischen Graden und Transkripte von Aufzeichnungen
• Kontaktinformationen von 1-2 früheren Beratern als Referenz
• Liste der Publikationen (fügen Sie Ihre Publikationen nicht in die PDF-Datei ein).
Die Bewerbungsfrist ist der 17. Januar 2027.
Mit uns schaffen Sie Werte.
Für dich und für die Gesellschaft.

## Beschreibung
Die Wiest-Gruppe der Abteilung für Gastroenterologie und Schleimhautimmunologie der Abteilung für biomedizinische Forschung der Universität Bern sucht einen Doktoranden, der an einem Projekt zur fettreichen Ernährung (HFD) induzierten Störung von Darmbarrieren arbeitet.
Unsere Gruppe interessiert sich für die Mechanismen, die zu Darmbarrierenbrüchen, pathologischer bakterieller Translokation bei Fettleibigkeit und Darm-Leber-Wechselwirkungen bei chronischen Lebererkrankungen führen, unter Verwendung einer breiten Palette von Techniken und Modellsystemen, die von Mausmodellen über Darmorganoidkulturen bis hin zu menschlichen Kohorten reichen (Castillo et al, 2026, PMID: 42521089; Wyss et al, 2026, PMID: 41999240).
Die Arbeit wird in enger Zusammenarbeit mit der Gruppe von Prof. Stephanie Ganal-Vonarburg, die die Auswirkungen von diätetischen und mikrobiellen Signalen auf die Darm- und Immunentwicklung im frühen Leben untersucht.

UniBE est interconnecté.
Avec nous, vous faites partie d'une communauté internationale et bénéficiez d'une collaboration interdisciplinaire.

## Description du projet et du poste
Ce projet de doctorat étudie la façon dont l'exposition au régime alimentaire riche en graisses perturbe la petite barrière intestinale et contribue au développement de la maladie du foie stéatotique associée au dysfonctionnement métabolique (MASL). À l'aide de modèles murins avancés, d'organoïdes intestinaux humains et de cultures cellulaires endothéliales intestinales, le projet vise à démêler les mécanismes moléculaires sous-jacents à la dysfonction barrière induite par le régime alimentaire, en mettant particulièrement l'accent sur la signalisation β-adrénergique et la perméabilité épithéliale et endothéliale. Combinant des expériences in vivo avec des tests de barrière fonctionnelle, des imageries et des analyses moléculaires, le projet explorera comment les graisses alimentaires altèrent l'intégrité et le fonctionnement de la barrière intestinale et pourrait identifier de nouvelles cibles thérapeutiques pour prévenir le dysfonctionnement de la barrière intestinale et sa contribution aux maladies métaboliques et hépatiques.
Des études seront menées au Département de recherche biomédicale (DBMR), dans les laboratoires de recherche de la division gastroentérologie/immunologie mucosale. Nous offrons un environnement de recherche hautement interdisciplinaire dédié à l'étude de l'immunologie muqueuse, du microbiote, de l'inflammation et du développement du cancer, impliquant le travail humain, les études animales et la biologie computationnelle, outre une supervision étroite et un grand esprit d'équipe.
Le paiement est fondé sur les règlements de financement de la Fondation nationale suisse des sciences (SNSF) pour les doctorants.

## Exigences
Les candidats sont titulaires d'un M. Sc. en immunologie, en microbiologie, en biologie moléculaire, en biotechnologie, en science animale ou dans tout domaine connexe en sciences biologiques. Comme le travail implique des expériences animales dans des conditions gnotobiotiques, un intérêt général pour ces techniques est nécessaire. Une excellente maîtrise de la langue anglaise (orale et écrite) est une exigence.
Soutien individuel aux carrières
Demande et contact
Veuillez envoyer votre candidature dans un seul fichier PDF nommé "application firstname.lastname" indiquant "PhD position" dans le sujet de l'email.
Le dossier doit comprendre :
• lettre d'accompagnement
• curriculum vitae (il doit avoir le format de date mm/aaaa)
• des copies des diplômes universitaires et des transcriptions des dossiers
• coordonnées de 1-2 conseillers précédents pour référence
• liste des publications (ne pas inclure vos publications dans le fichier pdf).
La date limite de présentation des demandes est le 17 janvier 2027.
Avec nous, vous créez de la valeur.
Pour vous-même et pour la société.

## Désignation des marchandises
Le groupe Wiest de la Division de gastroentérologie et d'immunologie mucosale du Département de recherche biomédicale de l'Université de Berne est à la recherche d'un doctorant pour travailler sur un projet sur le régime gras élevé (HFD) induit par la perturbation des barrières intestinales.
Notre groupe s'intéresse aux mécanismes menant à la rupture de la barrière intestinale, à la translocation pathologique des bactéries dans l'obésité et aux interactions intestinales dans les maladies hépatiques chroniques, en utilisant un large éventail de techniques et de systèmes modèles allant des modèles de souris, en passant par les cultures organoïdes intestinales aux cohortes humaines (Castillo et coll., 2026, PMID : 42521089; Wyss et coll., 2026, PMID : 41999240).
Les travaux seront menés en étroite collaboration avec le groupe de Prof. Stephanie Ganal-Vonarburg, qui étudie l'impact des signaux alimentaires et microbiens sur le développement intestinal et immunitaire au début de la vie.

## What We Offer
The University of Bern and the International Space Science Institute invite applications for two Postdoctoral research positions on star and planet formation in massive star clusters. Each position is for two years. The successful candidate will work with Professor Elena Sabbi and will have the opportunity to join several international collaborations. The successful candidates will analyze and interpret JWST and HST observations to address how massive star clusters form, and how massive stars affect the survival and evolution of protoplanetary disks in highly irradiated and/or low-metallicity environments in the Milky Way and the Magellanic Clouds.

• Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD in astronomy, astrophysics, or a related field by the start date. Previous experience with HST and JWST data is desirable, as is expertise in stellar and protoplanetary disk evolution and/or star cluster dynamics.

I candidati di successo analizzeranno e interpreteranno le osservazioni di JWST e HST per affrontare la forma di massicci ammassi stellari, e come le stelle massicce influiscono sulla sopravvivenza e sull'evoluzione dei dischi protoplanetari in ambienti altamente irradiati e/o a bassa metallicità nella Via Lattea e nelle Nuvole Magellaniche.

Die UniBE ist vernetzt.

## Deine Aufgaben
• Du arbeitest aktiv an der Planung und Durchführung der randomisiert-kontrollierten NEST-Bern-Studie mit
• Du rekrutierst und betreust Eltern-Kind-Paare im klinischen Setting
• Du führst standardisierte diagnostische und entwicklungspsychologische Assessments durch
• Du erhebst und wertest EMA-Daten sowie videobasierte Eltern-Kind-Interaktionen aus
• Du wirkst bei qualitativen Interviews und Mixed-Methods-Analysen mit
• Du bearbeitest eigenständig wissenschaftliche Fragestellungen im Rahmen deiner Dissertation
• Du publizierst wissenschaftliche Ergebnisse in internationalen Fachzeitschriften und präsentierst diese an nationalen und internationalen Kongressen

## Dein Profil
• Du verfügst über ein abgeschlossenes Masterstudium in Psychologie
• Du begeisterst dich für klinische Forschung, Entwicklungspsychologie und frühe Kindheit
• Du interessierst dich für digitale Medien und deren Auswirkungen auf die psychische Gesundheit
• Du hast Freude an der Arbeit mit Säuglingen, Kleinkindern und ihren Familien
• Du interessierst dich für quantitative und qualitative Forschungsmethoden
• Du bringst gute Statistikkenntnisse und erste praktische Erfahrungen in der Datenanalyse mit. Erfahrungen mit R oder vergleichbarer Statistiksoftware sind von Vorteil
• Du arbeitest selbstständig, strukturiert, zuverlässig und sorgfältig und schätzt die interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit
• Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse
Internationales Renommee
Bewerbung und Kontakt
Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung über den Button "Bewerben".
Bei uns schaffen Sie Wert.
Für sich und die Gesellschaft.

## Über uns
Forschung, die Familien bewegt – und die Zukunft unserer Kinder mitgestaltet!
Wie beeinflussen Smartphones, Tablets und andere digitale Medien die Entwicklung kleiner Kinder? Welche Rolle spielen Eltern bei der Regulation der Bildschirmzeit? Und wie können wir Familien dabei unterstützen, einen gesunden Umgang mit digitalen Medien zu entwickeln?
Diesen Fragen gehen wir im Forschungsprojekt NEST-Bern nach – und suchen Dich zur Verstärkung unseres Teams!
Das vom Schweizerischen Nationalfonds (SNF) mit über einer Million Franken geförderte Forschungsprojekt NEST-Bern untersucht die Wirksamkeit einer Eltern-Kind-Intervention zur Reduktion der Bildschirmzeit und Förderung der Selbstregulation bei Kindern im Alter von 0 bis 5 Jahren mit frühen psychischen Auffälligkeiten.
In einer randomisiert-kontrollierten Studie mit 300 Eltern-Kind-Paaren verbinden wir klinische Interventionsforschung mit innovativen Methoden wie Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA), videobasierten Eltern-Kind-Interaktionsbeobachtungen und qualitativen Interviews.
Das Projekt ist am Berner Eltern-Kind-Zentrum (BEK) angesiedelt und bietet die Möglichkeit, wissenschaftliche Forschung unmittelbar mit der klinischen Versorgung junger Kinder und ihrer Familien zu verbinden.
Wir bieten dir ein vielseitiges wissenschaftliches Umfeld, in dem du deine eigenen Forschungsfragen im Rahmen einer Promotion vertiefen und ein eigenständiges wissenschaftliches Profil entwickeln kannst. Dabei profitierst du von einer engen wissenschaftlichen Betreuung, Einblicken in innovative Forschungsmethoden und moderne Datenanalysen sowie der Förderung von Publikationen und der Teilnahme an nationalen und internationalen Kongressen. Deine Ideen sind willkommen und du kannst die Weiterentwicklung des Projekts aktiv mitgestalten.

## Informazioni su di noi
Ricerca che muove le famiglie – e plasma il futuro dei nostri figli!
Come fanno smartphone, tablet e altri media digitali a influenzare lo sviluppo dei bambini piccoli? Quale ruolo giocano i genitori nel regolare il tempo dello schermo? E come possiamo aiutare le famiglie a sviluppare un uso sano dei media digitali?
Perseguiamo queste domande nel progetto di ricerca NEST-Bern – e stiamo cercando di rafforzare il nostro team!
Il progetto di ricerca NEST-Bern, finanziato dalla Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) con più di un milione di franchi, indaga l'efficacia di un intervento genitore-figlio per ridurre il tempo dello schermo e promuovere l'auto-regolamentazione nei bambini di età compresa tra 0 e 5 anni con anomalie mentali anticipate.
In uno studio randomizzato-controllato di 300 coppie genitore-figlio, combiniamo la ricerca di intervento clinico con metodi innovativi come Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA), osservazioni video-based di interazione genitore-figlio e interviste qualitative.
Il progetto si trova presso il Centro genitori-bambini Bernesi (BEK) e offre l'opportunità di collegare direttamente la ricerca scientifica con la cura clinica dei bambini e delle loro famiglie.
Vi offriamo un ambiente scientifico versatile in cui è possibile approfondire le vostre domande di ricerca come parte di un dottorato e sviluppare un profilo scientifico indipendente. The UniBE is networked.
With us, you are part of an international community and benefit from interdisciplinary cooperation.

## Your tasks
• You are actively involved in the planning and implementation of the randomized-controlled NEST Berne study
• You recruit and support parent-child couples in clinical setting
• You conduct standardized diagnostic and developmental psychological assessments
• Collect and equip EMA data and video-based parent-child interactions
• You participate in qualitative interviews and mixed method analyses
• You work independently on scientific questions as part of your dissertation
• You publish scientific results in international journals and present them at national and international congresses

## Your profile
• You have a completed Master's degree in Psychology
• You are passionate about clinical research, developmental psychology and early childhood
• You are interested in digital media and its effects on mental health
• You enjoy working with infants, young children and their families
• You are interested in quantitative and qualitative research methods
• You bring good statistical knowledge and first practical experience in data analysis. Experience with R or comparable statistical software is an advantage
• You work independently, structured, reliable and carefully and appreciate the interdisciplinary cooperation
• You have very good knowledge of German and English
International reputation
Application and contact
We look forward to your application via the "Apply" button.
With us, you create value.
For themselves and society.

## About us
Research that moves families – and shapes the future of our children!
How do smartphones, tablets and other digital media affect the development of young children? What role do parents play in regulating screen time? And how can we help families develop a healthy use of digital media?
We pursue these questions in the research project NEST-Bern – and are looking for you to strengthen our team!
The research project NEST-Bern, funded by the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) with more than one million francs, investigates the effectiveness of a parent-child intervention to reduce screen time and promote self-regulation in children aged 0 to 5 years with early mental abnormalities.
In a randomized-controlled trial of 300 parent-child pairs, we combine clinical intervention research with innovative methods such as Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA), video-based parent-child interaction observations and qualitative interviews.
The project is located at the Bernese Parents-Child Center (BEK) and offers the opportunity to directly link scientific research with the clinical care of young children and their families.
We offer you a versatile scientific environment in which you can deepen your own research questions as part of a doctorate and develop an independent scientific profile. You will benefit from close scientific support, insights into innovative research methods and modern data analyses as well as the promotion of publications and participation in national and international congresses. Your ideas are welcome and you can actively shape the further development of the project.

Des recherches qui stimulent les familles – et façonnent l'avenir de nos enfants!
Comment les smartphones, tablettes et autres médias numériques affectent-ils le développement des jeunes enfants? Quel rôle les parents jouent - ils dans la régulation du temps d'écran? Et comment pouvons-nous aider les familles à développer une utilisation saine des médias numériques?
Nous poursuivons ces questions dans le projet de recherche NEST-Bern – et sommes à votre recherche pour renforcer notre équipe!
Le projet de recherche NEST-Bern, financé par la Fondation nationale suisse des sciences (SNSF) avec plus d'un million de francs, étudie l'efficacité d'une intervention parent-enfant pour réduire le temps de dépistage et promouvoir l'autorégulation chez les enfants de 0 à 5 ans souffrant d'anomalies mentales précoces.
Dans un essai contrôlé randomisé de 300 paires parents-enfants, nous combinons la recherche sur l'intervention clinique avec des méthodes novatrices telles que l'Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA), les observations d'interaction parents-enfants sur vidéo et les entrevues qualitatives.
Le projet est situé au Centre Bernois Parents-Enfants (BEK) et offre la possibilité de relier directement la recherche scientifique aux soins cliniques des jeunes enfants et de leur famille.
Nous vous offrons un environnement scientifique polyvalent dans lequel vous pouvez approfondir vos propres questions de recherche dans le cadre d'un doctorat et développer un profil scientifique indépendant. Vous bénéficierez d'un soutien scientifique étroit, d'un aperçu des méthodes de recherche novatrices et d'analyses de données modernes, ainsi que de la promotion des publications et de la participation aux congrès nationaux et internationaux. Vos idées sont les bienvenues et vous pouvez façonner activement le développement ultérieur du projet.

## Über uns
Wir bieten eine PhD-Stelle im Rahmen eines mit 1.99 Millionen CHF vom Schweizerischen Nationalfonds geförderten multizentrischen Projekts mit dem Titel «PRECISE-MDD: Precision Treatment Selection in Major Depressive Disorder Using EEG/ECG Biomarkers: A Multicenter Triple-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial with Clinical, Mechanistic, and Health-Economic Outcomes».
Die Studie wird am Universitären Psychiatrischen Zentrum Bern unter der Leitung von Prof. Dr. med. Tobias Bracht (Principal Investigator), Prof. Dr. Leila Soravia, und Prof. Dr. med. Bogdan Draganski durchgeführt. Weitere Studienzentren sind die Psychiatrischen Unikliniken in Zürich und in Basel. Ziel dieser multizentrischen, randomisiert-kontrollierten Studie ist es, den therapeutisch-prädiktiven Wert von EEG und EKG-basierten Biomarkern für unterschiedliche Behandlungsmodalitäten (Antidepressiva, rTMS, Ketamin, und EKT) bei Patientinnen und Patienten mit unipolarer Depression zu untersuchen. Die Studie basiert auf erfolgversprechenden Ergebnissen einer in Zürich durchgeführten, retrospektiven Studie. Am Studienzentrum Bern werden ergänzend, mit modernsten Methoden der Magnetresonanztomographie (MRT), Veränderungen der strukturellen und funktionellen Konnektivität im Gehirn ermittelt, welche in Zusammenhang mit einem Therapieansprechen stehen könnten. Alle MRT-Messungen finden am Swiss Institute for Translational and Entrepreneurial Medicine (SITEM) in Kooperation mit der Neuroradiologie am Inselspital in Bern statt.
Wir suchen eine Doktorandin/einen Doktoranden mit hoher Motivation und Interesse an klinischer sowie neurobiologischer Forschung im Bereich der affektiven Störungen. Die Stelle ist auf 4 Jahre befristet. ## I tuoi compiti

## Informazioni su di noi
Offriamo una posizione di dottorato nell'ambito di un progetto multicentro finanziato con 1,99 milioni di franchi dalla Fondazione Nazionale di Scienze Svizzera dal titolo "PRECISE-MDD: Selezione di trattamento di precisione nel Disturbo Depressivo Maggiore Utilizzando EEG/ECG Biomarkers: Un Trial di controllo randomizzato multicentrico a triplo filamento con risultati clinici, meccanici e economici della salute".
Lo studio è condotto presso il Centro Psichiatrico Universitario Berna sotto la direzione del Prof. Dottor Med. Tobias Bracht (Principal Investigator), Prof. Dr. Leila Soravia, e Prof. Dr. med. Bogdan Draganski eseguita. Ulteriori centri di studio sono le Cliniche Universitarie Psichiatriche di Zurigo e Basilea. L'obiettivo di questo studio multicentrico, randomizzato-controllato, è quello di indagare il valore terapeutico-predictive dei biomarcatori basati su EEG e ECG per diverse modalità di trattamento (antidepressivi, rTMS, ketamina e ECT) in pazienti con depressione unipolare. Lo studio si basa su risultati promettenti di uno studio retrospettivo condotto a Zurigo. Allo Studienzentrum Berna, oltre a metodi all'avanguardia di risonanza magnetica (MRI), si determinano cambiamenti nella connettività strutturale e funzionale nel cervello che potrebbero essere associati a una risposta terapeutica. Tutte le misurazioni della risonanza magnetica avvengono presso l'Istituto svizzero per la medicina traduttiva e imprenditoriale (SITEM) in collaborazione con la neuroradiologia dell'Inselspital di Berna.
Stiamo cercando uno studente di dottorato con alta motivazione e interesse nella ricerca clinica e neurobiologica nel campo dei disturbi affettivi. Il lavoro è limitato a 4 anni. Il team interdisciplinare e il finanziamento completo SNSF forniscono eccellenti opportunità strutturali per porre le basi per ulteriori carriere cliniche e/o scientifiche in neuropsichiatria, psichiatria clinica o psicologia.

## Your tasks

## About us
We offer a PhD position within the framework of a multicentre project funded with CHF 1.99 million by the Swiss National Science Foundation entitled "PRECISE-MDD: Precision Treatment Selection in Major Depressive Disorder Using EEG/ECG Biomarkers: A Multicenter Triple-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial with Clinical, Mechanistic, and Health-Economic Outcomes".
The study is conducted at the University Psychiatric Center Bern under the direction of Prof. Dr med. Tobias Bracht (Principal Investigator), Prof. Dr. Leila Soravia, and Prof. Dr. med. Bogdan Draganski performed. Further study centers are the Psychiatric University Clinics in Zurich and Basel. The aim of this multicenter, randomized-controlled study is to investigate the therapeutic-predictive value of EEG and ECG-based biomarkers for different treatment modalities (antidepressants, rTMS, ketamine, and ECT) in patients with unipolar depression. The study is based on promising results of a retrospective study conducted in Zurich. At the Studienzentrum Bern, in addition to state-of-the-art methods of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), changes in structural and functional connectivity in the brain are determined which could be associated with a therapy response. All MRI measurements take place at the Swiss Institute for Translational and Entrepreneurial Medicine (SITEM) in cooperation with Neuroradiology at Inselspital in Bern.
We are looking for a doctoral student with high motivation and interest in clinical and neurobiological research in the field of affective disorders. The job is limited to 4 years. The interdisciplinary team and comprehensive SNSF funding provide excellent structural opportunities to lay the foundation for further clinical and/or scientific careers in neuropsychiatry, clinical psychiatry or psychology.

Die UniBE ist ambitioniert.
Bei uns erbringen Sie Spitzenleistungen und messen sich mit den Besten.

## Sie bringen mit
• Schwerpunkt im Bereich Architekturgeschichte, idealerweise vor 1900
• Bereitschaft, Architekturgeschichte in einer grossen thematischen und zeitlichen Breite zu unterrichten (bspw. Einführung in die Architekturgeschichte)
• Bereitschaft zur Entwicklung eines Habilitationsprojekts im Bereich Architekturgeschichte, Architekturtheorie oder Denkmalpflege
• Bereitschaft zur Organisation von wissenschaftlichen Veranstaltungen und Exkursionen
• Freude an der Teamarbeit auf Augenhöhe in einem kollegialen, internationalen Umfeld
• Promotion (oder PhD) in Kunstgeschichte, Architekturgeschichte oder Architektur (Abschluss spätestens Sommer 2027)
• Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift; idealerweise gute Englisch- und Französischkenntnisse
• Teamfähigkeit
• Wohnsitz in der Schweiz oder Bereitschaft, in die Schweiz zu ziehen; im Semester ist der Arbeitsplatz in Bern mit max. 20% Homeoffice

## Wir bieten
• Eine voll finanzierte dreijährige Postdoktoratsstelle
• Die Möglichkeit, ein innovatives, eigenes Forschungsprojekt im Bereich der Architekturgeschichte zu entwickeln
• Ein inspirierendes Arbeitsumfeld am Institut für Kunstgeschichte
• Zugang zu nationalen und internationalen Forschungsnetzwerken, Archiven, Workshops, Tagungen und Weiterbildungsformaten
• Möglichkeiten zur Weiterentwicklung eigener Lehr- und Forschungsmethoden sowie des wissenschaftlichen Schreibens und Publizierens
• Anstellung und Lohn gemäss den Richtlinien der Universität Bern
• Hohe Lebensqualität im Kanton Bern mit vielfältigen Kultur- und Freizeitangeboten (Aareschwimmen, Wandern, Wintersport)
Kollaboratives Umfeld und ambitioniertes Team
Bewerbung und Kontakt
Bitte senden Sie Ihre Bewerbung in einer einzigen PDF-Datei an:
Bewerbungsfrist: 18. Januar 2027
Bewerbungsgespräche: 17.-19. Februar 2027
Die Bewerbung soll enthalten:
• Motivationsschreiben (max. 2 Seiten)
• Curriculum vitae mit Publikationsliste und Angaben zur Lehrerfahrung
• Zwei Referenzen, die vertraulich um ein Empfehlungsschreiben gebeten werden können
• BA-, MA- & Dissertationszeugnisse, gern mit Gutachten (falls vorhanden)
• Zwei repräsentative Arbeitsproben (z. B. Kapitel der Dissertation, veröffentlichter Artikel, Wissenschaftskommunikation, etc.)
• Beschreibung des Habilitationsprojekts (3-6 Seiten) & Angabe aktueller Stand der eigenen Forschung
Bei uns schaffen Sie Wert.
Für sich und die Gesellschaft.

## Wir suchen
Wir suchen eine:n Kandidat:in, die kurz vor der Promotion steht oder bereits über eine Dissertation in Kunstgeschichte, Kunstwissenschaften oder Architekturgeschichte oder Architektur verfügt. Gefordert ist ein inhaltlicher Schwerpunkt im Bereich der Geschichte und Theorie der Architektur, Baukultur oder Denkmalpflege (bspw. Europa, Süd/Osteuropa, Lateinamerika, MENA-Region), idealerweise im Zeitraum vor 1900. Dieser Schwerpunkt soll die Abteilung in Forschung und Lehre ergänzen und erweitern. Die Tätigkeit umfasst die Entwicklung eines eigenen Habilitationsprojekts (50%), Lehrtätigkeit auf BA-Stufe (2-4 SWS), Beteiligung an den wissenschaftlichen Aktivitäten der Abteilung (Exkursionen, Konferenzen, Publikationen) sowie administrative Tätigkeiten. Die Arbeitssprachen sind Deutsch und Englisch; sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift sind verpflichtend.

Job-Abo
Bewerbungsablauf

## Ihre Benefits
Interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit
Internationales Renommee

Die Universität Bern bietet nicht nur spannende Aufgaben, sondern auch ein Umfeld, das Entwicklung, Vielfalt und Chancengleichheit aktiv fördert. Entdecken Sie, was uns als Arbeitgeberin auszeichnet und wie Sie bei uns weiterkommen.

descriptionByLocale.it:
L'UniBE è ambizioso.
Con noi, eseguono l'eccellenza e competono con il meglio.

## Portano con loro
• Focus sulla storia architettonica, idealmente prima del 1900
• Volontà di insegnare la storia architettonica in una vasta larghezza tematica e temporale (per esempio introduzione alla storia architettonica)
• Volontà di sviluppare un progetto di abilitazione nel campo della storia architettonica, della teoria architettonica o della conservazione del patrimonio
• Volontà di organizzare eventi scientifici ed escursioni
• Godetevi il lavoro di squadra a livello degli occhi in un ambiente collegiale e internazionale
• Dottorato (o PhD) in Storia dell'Arte, Storia dell'Architettura o Architettura (grado non oltre l'estate 2027)
• Molto buona conoscenza del tedesco in parola e scrittura; Idealmente buone abilità inglesi e francesi
• Lavoro di squadra
• residenza in Svizzera o disponibilità a trasferirsi in Svizzera; nel semestre, il posto di lavoro a Berna è con max. 20% home office

## Offriamo
• Una posizione post-doctoral di tre anni completamente finanziata
• L'opportunità di sviluppare un progetto di ricerca innovativo e proprio nel campo della storia architettonica
• Un ambiente di lavoro stimolante presso l'Istituto di Storia dell'Arte
• Accesso a reti di ricerca nazionali e internazionali, archivi, workshop, incontri e formati di formazione
• Opportunità per l'ulteriore sviluppo dei propri metodi di insegnamento e di ricerca, nonché scrittura scientifica e pubblicazione
• Occupazione e salari secondo le linee guida dell'Università di Berna
• Alta qualità della vita nel Cantone di Berna con diverse attività culturali e ricreative (zona nuoto, escursioni, sport invernali)
Ambiente collaborativo e team ambizioso
Applicazione e contatto
Invia la tua richiesta in un unico file PDF a:
Termine per la richiesta: 18. gennaio 2027
Interviste di lavoro: 17.-19. Febbraio 2027
La domanda comprende:
• Lettera di motivazione (max. 2 pagine)
• Curriculum vitae con elenco pubblicazioni e informazioni sull'esperienza didattica
• Due riferimenti che possono essere confidenziali richiesti per una lettera di raccomandazione
• Certificati BA, MA e dissertazione, con opinioni esperte (se disponibili)
• Due campioni di lavoro rappresentativi (ad esempio capitolo della dissertazione, articolo pubblicato, comunicazione scientifica, ecc.)
• Descrizione del progetto di abilitazione (3-6 pagine) & indicazione dello stato attuale della propria ricerca
Con noi, crei valore.
Per se stessi e per la società.

## Stiamo cercando
Siamo alla ricerca di un candidato: in chi sta per ricevere un dottorato o già ha una dissertazione nella storia dell'arte, studi d'arte o storia architettonica o architettura. Ciò che è necessario è un focus sulla storia e la teoria dell'architettura, della cultura edile o della conservazione del patrimonio (ad esempio Europa, Sud/Est Europa, America Latina, regione MENA), idealmente nel periodo prima del 1900. Questo focus è destinato a integrare e ampliare il dipartimento nella ricerca e nell'insegnamento. L'attività comprende lo sviluppo di un proprio progetto di abilitazione (50%), l'insegnamento a livello BA (2-4 SWS), la partecipazione alle attività scientifiche del dipartimento (escursioni, conferenze, pubblicazioni) e le attività amministrative. Le lingue di lavoro sono tedesche e inglesi; la buona conoscenza del tedesco in parola e la scrittura è obbligatoria.

The UniBE is ambitious.
With us, they perform excellence and compete with the best.

## They bring with them
• Focus on architectural history, ideally before 1900
• Willingness to teach architectural history in a broad thematic and temporal breadth (e.g. introduction to architectural history)
• Willingness to develop a habilitation project in the field of architectural history, architectural theory or heritage conservation
• Willingness to organise scientific events and excursions
• Enjoying teamwork at eye level in a collegial, international environment
• Doctorate (or PhD) in History of Art, History of Architecture or Architecture (degree no later than summer 2027)
• Very good knowledge of German in word and writing; Ideally good English and French skills
• Teamwork
• residence in Switzerland or willingness to move to Switzerland; in the semester, the workplace in Bern is with max. 20% home office

## We offer
• A fully funded three-year postdoctoral position
• The opportunity to develop an innovative, own research project in the field of architectural history
• An inspiring working environment at the Institute of Art History
• Access to national and international research networks, archives, workshops, meetings and training formats
• Opportunities for the further development of own teaching and research methods as well as scientific writing and publishing
• Employment and wages according to the guidelines of the University of Bern
• High quality of life in the Canton of Bern with diverse cultural and leisure activities (area swimming, hiking, winter sports)
Collaborative environment and ambitious team
Application and contact
Please send your application in a single PDF file to:
Application deadline: 18. January 2027
Job interviews: 17.-19. February 2027
The application shall include:
• Letter of motivation (max. 2 pages)
• Curriculum vitae with publication list and teaching experience information
• Two references that can be confidentially asked for a letter of recommendation
• BA, MA and dissertation certificates, with expert opinions (if available)
• Two representative work samples (e.g. chapter of the dissertation, published article, science communication, etc.)
• Description of the habilitation project (3-6 pages) & indication of current status of own research
With us, you create value.
For themselves and society.

## We are looking for
We are looking for a:n candidate:in who is about to receive a doctorate or already has a dissertation in art history, art studies or architectural history or architecture. What is required is a focus on the history and theory of architecture, building culture or heritage conservation (e.g. Europe, South/East Europe, Latin America, MENA region), ideally in the period before 1900. This focus is intended to complement and expand the department in research and teaching. The activity includes the development of an own habilitation project (50%), teaching at BA level (2-4 SWS), participation in the scientific activities of the department (excursions, conferences, publications) and administrative activities. The working languages shall be German and English; very good knowledge of German in word and writing is mandatory.
